articleTitle: Dielectric Properties of Water Solutions with Small Content of Glucose in the Millimeter - Wave Band and the Determination of Glucose in Blood
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, dielectric properties of glucose solutions, blood and skin have been measured in the frequency range from 28 to 93 GHz. These measurements have shown that using millimeter waves it is possible to realize nondestructive a real-time determination small content of sugar (glucose) content in so solutions and one drop of blood, as well as to develop after some additional investigations noninvasive method for glucose content monitoring through skin.

articleTitle: Low-Noise, High Dynamic Range Digital Receiver/Spectrometer for Radio Astronomy Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, a recently developed digital receiver which satisfies to a large extent the modern requirements to such devices is presented. This receiver has been tested at the decameter radio telescope UTR-2. It is well known that the negative impact of radio frequency interference (RFI) on the quality of data is a matter of increasing concern especially for the low frequency radio astronomy.

articleTitle: The Signal Digital Processing in the Millimeter Band FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The frequency-modulated continuous wave-radars - (FMCW-radars) are widely applied in the car road safety systems, the aircraft altimeters, the fusion plasma microwave diagnostics and in other ranging systems of different usage. The most optimal choice in terms of the "cost-quality" criterion for the radars that function at tens of meters distances is a transceiving set homodyne circuitry preference. The Gunn oscillators and Schottky diode barrier mixers usage in such radar sets let one create solid-state midget microwave detectors of different purposes. However, designing the transceiving set-based measuring system, one is confronted with a number of difficulties, depended on the high requirements over the transmitted waveshape and the generator and reception path gain frequency responses linearity.

articleTitle: Implementation of Noise Radar Technology in Ground Based SAR for Short Range Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, results of implementation of noise radar technology in X-band narrowband ground based (GB) synthetic aperture radar (SAR) were presented. The radars under consideration use noise waveform (NW) as a probe signal and perform the range focusing by correlating the radar returns with a reference signal taken before transmission, while the way the azimuth compression is done is similar to that of the conventional SAR. Evaluation of the phase measurements precision with the help of GB NW SAR was carried out on the basis of the obtained interferograms. It has been shown that both NW SAR systems provide quite high precision of displacement measurements.It was also demonstrated that noise radar technology may provide rather high performance of radar designed for short range applications with interferometric capabilities including ground based SAR and d-InSAR systems.

articleTitle: The Millimetr and Submillimetr Waves Generators and Amplifiers on Wavy Bent Rectangular Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The mathematical model of BWO and TWT on wavy bent rectangular waveguides with the use of equivalent quadripoles is presented. Results of optimizations calculations of BWO and TWT in a frequency range 37...3000 GHz are represented. Research of influence of the dimensions of a waveguide, losses, the dimensions of an electron beam on characteristics of devices are carried out.

articleTitle: New Mobile Ground-Based Microwave Instrument to Research of Stratospheric Ozone (Some Results of Observations)
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Millimeter-wave spectrometers are considered now as the most actual instruments for monitoring stratospheric ozone and other minor gas constituents . All results were obtained using microwave technique which has big dimensions, complicate antenna system and can not be easy transported to the other site of observation. Some scientific tasks require the development of portable microwave instrument for ozone measurements and new approach for design. In the paper, we present some recent results which were obtained with the help of the new microwave device [6].

articleTitle: Development of a Ka-Band Slotted Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: An effective approach to the design of planar slotted array has been presented in the paper. The approach has been successfully used for the development of the described Ka-band antenna for airborne radar applications. A high reproducibility of the antenna characteristics have been observed along with a high degree of their compliance with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Conception of Scaling, Fractional Dimension and Deterministic Chaos in Radio Physics and Radio Electronics
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: It has been briefly reported how the new synergetic approach on the basis of fractional measuring, fractal dimension, scaling, fractals and deterministic chaos has been developing in IRE RAS as applied to problems of modern non-linear radio physics and radio engineering.New challenging information technologies development and introduction on the basis of fractal radio physics and fractal radio electronics principles relates with training of specialists for these scientific fields.

articleTitle: Terahertz Self-Oscillations in Avalanche P-N Junction with DC Current Injection
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, computer simulation results for the self-oscillations of currents flowing through a reverse biased p-n junction with DC current injection were presented. Results showed that such self-oscillatory regime is promising to build a new auto-generator operating in terahertz frequency band.

articleTitle: High Temperature Superconducting Microwave Filters for Applications in Mobile Communication, Satellite Receiver and Wind-Profile Radar
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Three types of high performance high temperature superconducting (HTS) filters for different applications are introduced. The HTS filter for 3G mobile base station, which is constructed by multi-loop resonators, showed ultra selectivity with extremely small fractional bandwidth (narrower than 0.23%), extremely steep skirt slope (140- 220 dB/MHz) and excellent out-of-band rejections. The integrated bandpass and bandstop HTS filters for satellite receiver made by YBCO and TBCCO thin films achieved very small return loss (≤-22.5 dB) and extremely high out-of-band rejection at certain frequency bands (> 110 dB) simultaneously and showed satisfactory results in the space qualification mechanical tests. Field tests of the wind-profile radar exhibited that with HTS subsystem an increase of 3.7 dB in sensitivity and an improvement of 48.4 dB in anti-interference ability of the radar were attained so that when conventional radar failed to detect the speed and direction of the wind above 2000 meters of the radar due to interference, the HTS radar can produce perfect wind spectrums and profiles.

articleTitle: Modes Excitation in Diffraction Radiation Oscillator on High Space Harmonics of the Periodic Structure
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The present report discusses experimental results obtained in an effort to compare the diffraction radiation oscillator operation features in the case of the excitation on the first, second and third space harmonics of the reflecting diffraction grating accommodated in the interior of the same open resonant system (ORS). It will be shown that a reasonable ORS choice provides the DRO excitation on the high-order space harmonics nearly without the starting current growth.

articleTitle: Dual-Layer Frequency-Selective Subwavelength-Grid Polarizers for THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In our work, we perform numerical simulations of multi-layer subwavelength grid THz polarizers and evaluate their efficiency as a function of various design parameters.

articleTitle: A Waveform Receiver for Continuous Registration of Fast Processes in Pulsar Radio Emission
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This paper presents the investigation of fast processes in radio emission of pulsars, magnetars, RRATs, etc. demands a long continuous recording with high time resolution. Now pulse radio emissions from magnetosphere of different kind of neutron stars are observed in the range from decameter wave length up to 40 GHz. In the lowest one - decameter wave range it's very difficult to achieve high time resolution due to effects of scattering and dispersive delay of the pulse propagation in the interstellar medium (ISM) which lead to the broadening of pulse signal in the receiving band. In spectral receivers, real time digital receivers with fast Fourier transform (FFT) or in the filter bank analyzers time resolution is determined by the pulse broadening in the frequency band of a single digital channel. The analogue part of the receiver - amplifiers and mixers for the work under high level of interference have been worked off long ago in the equipment developed in the RINAN of Ukraine for the radio telescopes UTR-2 and URAN.

articleTitle: Near-Field Millimeter Wave and Microwave Tomography Imaging
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A near-field millimeter-wave tomography system has been designed and built for imaging of hidden objects located in subsurface areas of different materials and fabrics. In our investigations we used conceptions of near-field microscopy and subsurface tomography. The algorithm is based on the integral representation of the scattered field at the probing line above a lossy half-space containing a cylindrical object of arbitrary cross-section and electrical properties in the case of plane wave incidence. The object function is related to 1D Fourier transform of the measured scattered field by the tomography integral equation. For image reconstruction of objects a part of the spatial spectrum of the scattered field due to nonuniform or evanescent waves was employed.

articleTitle: Influence of Random Bulk Inhomogeneities on Quasioptical Cavity Resonator Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, the physical nature of the broadening and the shift of spectral lines of the quasi-optical cavity resonator filled with randomly distributed bulk inhomogeneities has been studied both theoretically and experimentally. The inhomogeneities quasioptical cavity millimeter wave resonator (passive and active) can serve as model of semiconductor quantum billiard. Based on our results we suggest using quantum billiard with spectrum rarefied by random inhomogeneities as an active system of semiconductor laser.

articleTitle: Near-Field Plane Distribution of Rectangular Waveguide Excited by Dominant and Higher-Order Modes
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, on the basis of Hertz potential technique, the expressions for calculation of the radiation field of aperture antennas with given distribution of field sources in rectangular coordinate system were obtained in the closed form. Derived expressions allow to calculate amplitude, phase and polarization radiation characteristics of canonical radiators, rectangular waveguide and pyramidal horn, on the planes at the different distances from the aperture to the point of observation. The calculation of radiation characteristics was carried out for the case of waveguide excitation by dominant TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> mode and for the case of TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub> and TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</sub> higher order mode excitation. The analysis of field distribution at the near-field reactive and "very-near-field" zones was performed. It was shown that for electrically small rectangular waveguides excited by TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> mode the boundary of far- zone can be defined as 1.8-2.0lambda with satisfactory for practice accuracy. Knowledge of complex amplitude value in near zone for waveguide with separate TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m0</sub> mode excitation allows to obtain the amplitude and phase near zone characteristics of the waveguide with multimode excitation, for example TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> + TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub>, TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub> + TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</sub>, TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub> + TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</sub> and so on excited at the same frequency.

articleTitle: Whispering Gallery Mode Sapphire Resonator for Microwave Characterization of Lossy Liquids
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Whispering gallery mode (WGM) resonators are used widely for electrophysical parameter determination of different substances. Earlier it was shown that radially two-layered resonator made of Teflon can be used for complex permittivity measurement of lossy liquids. The resonator was a Teflon ring sandwiched between conducting endplates (CEP). Substances measured were distilled water and ethyl alcohol. They were put into interior layer of resonator. It is worth to note that accuracy of lossy liquid (such as water) measurement by means of Teflon resonator is insufficient. Evidently, for increasing accuracy of complex permittivity measurement a complex permittivity of outer layer in the resonator must be higher than permittivity of Teflon.

articleTitle: Microwave Photonics Applications of Whispering Gallery Mode Resonators
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Whispering gallery resonators (WGRs) made of electro-optic crystals are suitable for the realization of widely tunable microwave photonic filters as well as electro-optical modulators. We review recent progress in the field and discuss possible solutions of problems related to design and fabrication of narrow-band widely tunable high- order filters based on high-Q LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> WGRs and demonstrate fifth-order filter function with the resonators.

articleTitle: Determination of Oscillation Parameters of Open Resonator Systems using Fractional-Rational Approximation by Continued Fraction
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Open resonators (OR) are one of basic elements of modern systems and devices of millimeter and submillimeter wavelength ranges. The one-port network presentation of the coupling OR, and processing of the measurements of complex reflection coefficient by linear-fractional approximation allows one to determine oscillation parameters of single resonance in open resonance systems at presence of radiation losses in coupling ports.

articleTitle: Development of the Orotrons at Millimeter and Submillimeter Wavelength Range
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, the low-voltage pulse orotron generators of the short millimeter and long submillimeter waves with power level up to 1 W have been developed. Some methods of frequency and power enhancement are proposed.

articleTitle: Open Resonators for Millimeter Wave Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This paper discusses two versions of resonator that appear well suited for millimetre wave applications. The first proposed solution is given by the whispering gallery mode (WGM) dielectric resonator. The second proposed solution is a variant of the so called nonradiative configuration (nonradiative metallic resonator). The key element of both the proposed solutions is given by their open configuration, namely by a configuration not completely shielded by metallic surfaces.

articleTitle: Microwave Imager/Sounder MTVZA-GY of Spacecraft "Meteor-M"
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The following paper describes the microwave imager/sounder MTVZA-GY of spacecraft "Meteor-M". The spacecraft will be launched in 2008 on Sun synchronous orbit at an altitude of 830 km. MTVZA-GY will be used as the meteorological imaging/sounding system for remote sensing of ocean and land surface, as well as, for measuring global atmospheric temperature and water vapor profiles. The instrument is the next version of microwave imager/sounder MTVZA deployed on spacecraft "Meteor-3M" and MTVZA-OK deployed on spacecraft "Sich-IM".

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Frequency Selective Surfaces Perforated with Arbitrarily Shaped Apertures
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: We have proposed a method for the electromagnetic analysis of FSS perforated with arbitrary shaped apertures. It is based on the boundary integral equation method, mode matching technique and S- matrix method and has been implemented in a computer code. The data calculated by the code is in accordance with published ones. Furthermore, we have shown the influence of possible fabrication inaccuracies on transmission properties of the FSS.

articleTitle: Whispering-Gallery Mode Resonators for Liquid Droplet Detection
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Whispering-gallery mode (WGM) dielectric resonators provide compact design, high mechanical stability and high quality factors from microwaves up to frequencies in the visible range. In particular, the specific dielectric response of liquids in micro- and (sub)millimetre wave frequency bands (10 GHz to 3 THz) make WGM mode resonators and resonator arrays in this frequency range attractive for highly sensitive liquid detection and identification of small droplets down to volumes of picolitres. Since droplets are usually generated by computer controlled microinjection pipettes being moved on a 2D scanning table, free access to the sensitive resonator surface from above is essential.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of UWB Electromagnetic Pulses Propagation in Dispersive Electrodynamic Lines
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This paper considers a computer simulation method for ultrawideband (UWB) pulse fields excited in a regular electrodynamic line by either a short external current or by a bunched electron beam. The high-frequency components of the radio pulse move more rapidly than the low-frequency ones, the first overtake the latter after some time. The delay line does not transmit the low-frequency components of the video pulse at all, so this turns into a radio pulse gradually passing some distance.

articleTitle: Phenomena of Resonant Transmission through Perforated Metal Plates
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, several structures that allow for optical, terahertz, and microwave enhanced transmission phenomena through metal plates perforated by arrays of holes of subwavelength cross-section are investigated. It is shown that the transmission enhancement is associated with resonant coupling between the incident/transmitted field and source-free fields supported by the perforated plate. The source-free fields are allowed when any type of slow waves is supported by the plate and a proper periodic arrangement of the subwavelength holes is present.

articleTitle: Improved Noise Parametr Estimation and Filtering of MM-Band SLAR Images
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Blind (automatic) techniques for determination of noise characteristics of Ka- and X-band SLAR images obtained from the Institute of Radiophysics and Electronics of UNAS and A.I. Kalmukov Center of Earth Radiophysical Sensing. New modification on a filter based on a discrete cosine transform applied in sliding blocks is described. Filter efficiency is considerably improved by taking into account noise type and statistical characteristics.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave Imaging System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Passive imaging systems at millimeter wave (MMW) radio band are in the limelight at the past few years. Passive MMW imaging systems have some essential advantages connecting with high spatial resolution realized at relatively small antenna aperture sizes, secretive mode of operation, lack of operational distance limitations, lack of emitting electromagnetic fields capable cause negative effect on surrounding people and attendant staff. In passive imaging at MMW band one effective method of antenna beam monitoring was invented more then 25 years ago and consisted in scanning antenna realization on the principles of volume-to-surface wave transformation at open electrodynamics systems.

articleTitle: New Concept of Multiplex Broadband Wireless Communication for Vehicle-to-Vehicle Data Transmission on Highways
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, a new approach is proposed to design a vehicle-to-vehicle data transmission (VVDT) system within the dedicated short-range communications (DSRC) concept capable of data transmitting in real-time scale between all cars within a highway area of 1 km radius. The method suggested makes possible a multi-frequency carrier and space-code division multiple access (MC-S-CDMA) and principle implementation of information transmitting with usage of broadband chaotic waveform codes. Combination of frequency and CDMA channels separation and chaotic waveform coding for implementing CDMA standard are distinguishing features of the suggested DSRC-WDT system. A new method for code prescribed to each car within the working range of DSRC-VVDT system enables usage of identical standard Tx/Rx equipment for all vehicles.

articleTitle: THz-Range Spatial-Harmonic Magnetrons
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The numerical simulation has been used to determine the tentative parameters submm- wavelength SHMs. The reliability of the developed 3-D models is evidenced by the results from testing of the operating laboratory prototypes of the THz-range thermionic-cathode SHMs. The 3-D model thus created can be used in developing the small-size THz-range cold secondary-emission SHMs. The concept of drift-orbital resonance in SHMs allows testing the basic parameters of THz-range magnetrons. It can be used to develop the submm-wavelength spatial-harmonic magnetrons. It can be used to develop the submm-wavelength spatial-harmonics magnetrons.

articleTitle: A High Selective HTS Filter with Group Delay Self-Equalization for 3G Mobile Telecommunication Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A recent development of a twelve-pole high-temperature-superconducting (HTS) bandpass filter with group delay self-equalization for 3G wireless applications is reported. The filter is designed to have a 5.425 MHz pass-band at a centre frequency of 2121.5 MHz. The filter exhibits a quasi-elliptic function response implemented with a cascaded quadruplet (CQ) coupling structure. Two pair of complex frequency transmission zeros have been introduced to implement linear phase for group delay self-equalization. The filter was fabricated on a 0.5 mm-thick MgO wafer with double-sided YBCO films. The filter displayed a minimum insertion loss of 0.2 dB in the passband and a return loss better than 14 dB over the pass-band. Out-of-band rejection at both sides is higher than 57 dB with the skirt-slope as high as 100 MHz. The filter shows a 60 ns fluctuation of group delay within 78% pass-band which matches the requirement of TD-SCDMA standard of 3G mobile telecommunication.

articleTitle: Detecting Defects of Leather Material on the Base of Radiometric Method in MM-Wave Band
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Leather material blemish zone detection and registration of areas suitable for next utilization are actual tasks in leather manufacturing branch. Ultra-high frequency (UHF) radiometric method of leather material diagnostic should be applied as a prospective solution on this way. With the aim of radiometric method potential abilities evaluation in leather materials diagnostic, a set of laboratory measurements of radiothermal radiation total loss factor was realized in microwave and millimeter wave bands for prime product of leather material, which is ordinarily obtained in the initial stage of cattle skin treatment. It is possible to declare that radiation optimal wavelength, which will be correlated with maximum brightness contrasts between defect and condition areas in inspecting leather material will be gradually drifted towards to shorter millimeter wavelength for observed diagnostic method.

articleTitle: Static and Dynamic Hysteresis Loops in Samples of Uniaxial Barium Hexaferrite
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The hysteresis of frequency-field dependence was experimentally investigated and these data compared with the local hysteresis curves of magnetization for epitaxial films and bulk monocrystal plates BaFe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sub>. It is shown that these data are correlated and the measured values of the fields of break H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">br</sub> are coincided in both cases. It is found that the phenomenon of hysteresis FMR was caused by the delay of generation and growth of magnetic reversal centers. It was offered to use the character of transition from the saturated region to one domain as a criterion of the epitaxial films quality.

articleTitle: Classification of Masses in Mammography Images Using Wavelet Transform and Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this work, a method for masses and microcalcifications (MCs) classification in the mammography (MG) images was presented. The procedure consists of applying wavelet transform (WT), regions segmentation and multilayer neural network type classifiers. The implemented scheme permits to reduce the iterations number during the training of the neural network MLP applying WT. We adapted Daubechies, Symlet, Coiflet and biorthogonal functions using MLP network for microcalcifications classification in the MG images. The experimental results have shown good performance of the implemented algorithms.

articleTitle: Resonant Stratified Cylindrical Structures with Time Discontinuity in Permittivity
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper we consider the transformation of whispering gallery modes (WGM) of circular dielectric resonators due to temporal changes in permittivity inside the concentric circular region. We explore how the transients evolve from the complex interaction of reflections occurring at the dielectric interfaces. A closed form solution is obtained for the electric field component by applying the Laplace transform directly to the wave equation and enforcing the corresponding initial and boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Influence of Electromagnetic Radiation on the Seeds of Technical Plants and the Blood of Man
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, the influence of microwave radiation on the germination of rape seeds was presented. Also, biological effects of microwave radiation on blood was determined for the investigation of immunological indexes.

articleTitle: Features of Formation of Dispersion Spectrum of Semiconductor-Dielectric Periodic Structure in Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, the peculiarity of the zone spectrum formation of the semiconductor-dielectric periodic structure in the magnetic field when omega<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sub> > omega<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">P</sub> was investigated. Main result of our work is that we have proposed and have proved a method of separation of the periodic structure full spectrum into structure eigen modes. It is based on the analysis of the field distribution in the vicinity of the crossing or touching regions.

articleTitle: Laminates of Thin Ferromagnetic Films for Microwave Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Thin ferromagnetic films are known to exhibit the highest possible microwave permeability of known magnetic materials. Magnetic materials with high microwave magnetic performance are useful for many technical applications. However, bulk rather than planar materials are frequently needed for the applications. Bulk materials with high microwave permeability may be produced as laminated structures of thin ferromagnetic films, possibly patterned. The paper presents experimental data on the microwave permeability of such laminated structures based on Fe films. Possible technical applications of the materials under study include thin wideband radar absorbers and miniaturized patch antennas.

articleTitle: Diffraction Radiation Oscillator with Resonant Matching of Diffraction Grating in Open Resonator
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The diffraction grating (DG) is the important component of the open resonant system (ORS) used in diffraction radiation oscillator (DRO). The amplitude-phase distribution behavior of the DG space harmonics in a frequency band determines the power and spectral DRO characteristics in many respects. The space harmonics amplitude of DG depends on matching of DG with ORS field. Earlier the problem of the matching of an open resonator field with inhomogeneity in the form of DG was resolved by several ways: one of the open resonator mirrors was completely covered by the DG (orotron), the phase matching of a grating with ORS field was achieved due to rising of the restricted DG above a smooth part of a mirror.

articleTitle: New Terahertz Mixer Based on Resonant-Tunneling Diode
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This work shows that the electron transport mechanism in a resonant-tunneling diode (RTD) define RTD noise properties and it's operation speed. Optimization for two types of heterostructures: matched - In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.53</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.47</sub>As/In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.52</sub>Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.48</sub>As and pseudomorphic -In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.53</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.47</sub>As/AlAs, are carried out. Results show that properly designed RTD will have essential nonlinearity at zero bias and can be successfully employed as an active element of terahertz subharmonic mixer.

articleTitle: Performance of Falcon-I: Developed Low-Power and High-Sensitivity Cloud Profiling FM-CW Radar at 95GHz
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: We have developed a low-power and high-sensitivity cloud profiling radar, named FALCON-I, transmitting frequency modulated continuous wave (FM-CW) at 95 GHz for ground-based observations. Millimeter wave at 95 GHz is used to realize much higher sensitivity than lower frequencies to small cloud particles. An FM-CW type radar realizes similar sensitivity with much smaller output power to a pulse type radar. Two lm- diameter parabolic antennas separated by 1.4 m each other are used for transmitting and receiving the wave. The direction of the antennas is fixed at the zenith at this moment. The radar can observe clouds up to 20 km in height with the range resolution of 15 m and the angular resolution of 0.2 degree. Simultaneous observations of FALCON-I and a pulse type radar, SPIDER, show good performance of FALCON-I. Sensitivity of FALCON-I is -32 dBZ in radar reflectivity factor at 5 km, which is only 3 dB worse than that of SPIDER although its output power is 1/3000 to SPIDER. Ranging resolution of 15 m is realized for FALCON-I, which is 1/10 of that of SPIDER. Using developed FALCON-I, we observed clouds in various regions and oceans in the last three years.

articleTitle: Selective Excitation of the High-Order Modes in the Waveguide Quasioptical Resonator
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The method of a spatial Fourier filtration for selective excitation of separate higher types of oscillations with a high degree of discrimination of undesirable modes is proposed and realized. By the matrix method it is carried out a numerical study of characteristics of the lowest transverse modes for the metal resonator of the submillimeter laser from the geometrical sizes of mirrors and parameters of the amplitude-stepped filter in the form of absorbing elements disposed in nodal lines of a field for selected modes in the region of their spatial frequencies on the nonuniform mirror of SDM. Our investigations showed that in the metal resonator for excitation of a higher type of oscillation with circular polarization TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub> the Fresnel number N should make 1.5 - 1.6, and for excitation of a higher type of oscillation TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</sub> is N> 2. The additional losses introduced by absorbing elements in the selected mode, do not exceed 0.5 - 3 % at change of their relative width within the limits of radiuses 0.04 - 0.14 for the flat mirror of SDM. Thus the difference of energy losses for selected TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub> and TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</sub> modes and nearest on losses discriminated modes is given not less than 20 %.

articleTitle: Ground-Based Noise Waveform SAR and Differential Interferometry for Remote Monitoring of Large Objects
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The work is dedicated to experimental investigation of parameters of this SAR. A brief overview of SAR system is given; measurement set-up and estimation results of both accuracy and phase stability are described.

articleTitle: Electromagnetism of Artificial Fractal Medium - The Physico-Geometrical Groundwork
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The algorithms suggested in this paper for introducing the physico-geometric information relate both to solutions of integral Maxwell's equations for problems characterized by charge and current distributions at fractal interfaces between media, and the differential Helmholtz equation with boundary conditions obtained according to the scheme given. We have studied and analysed a new class of artificial waveguides, which can be made of cylindrical waveguides containing homogeneous isotropic artificial materials.

articleTitle: Low-Noise pHEMT Amplifier Operating at Extra-Low Supply Voltage and Power
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: We report on the successful development of an extra-low supply single-drain-operated amplifier intended for use as a general-purpose LNA for the practical frequency band over 1.5 to 2.5 GHz. It is a two-stage amplifier based on cost-effective commercial pHEMTs. The amplifier design and performance is discussed.

articleTitle: Planar Waveguides and Resonators of MM- and SubMM Bands
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, theoretical and experimental investigation of the electrodynamic processes with TEM waveguide of different geometries (filter-coupler, near-field probe, band-stop filter) were presented. The investigation showed that a wide-band planar waveguiding structures can be constructed on basis of the TEM two-strip waveguide. Due to construction and development simplicity of a TEM two-strip waveguide it can be used not only in millimetre but in sub-millimetre, terahertz and even in optical wave-range. Achievement of near-field probe such higher electrical field amplitude at the apex signified that this probe can be used to create near-field probes for optical data recording and spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Oscillations of Radiation of Solar Flares in 3 mm Range
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The radio emission of the Sun in 3-mm range observations are the important source of the information about dynamics of evolution of solar active regions. The solar flares observations allow investigation the physical processes accompanying these phenomena. Their variety determines uniqueness of each solar flare. Solar flares are the result of abundant magnetic field annihilation during magnetic lines reconnection. Abundant magnetic field energy accumulation occurs at the vortex motion of the magnetized plasma of photosphere due to pressing a magnetic field and the stretching of magnetic tubes. The magnetic lines of a various direction approach results in appearance of the high-power current layers between them for compensation a tangential gap. Current layers dissipate at reconnection of magnetic lines. It causes flare high- temperature heating of plasma in the field of magnetic reconnection. Thus there are an acceleration of free electrons up to high energy and electromagnetic energy radiation by them in broad frequency band.

articleTitle: Radially Three-Layered Dielectric Resonators for Millimeter Wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In the present paper eigen oscillations of radially three-layered cylindrical and spherical dielectric resonators are studied. The cylindrical resonator is limited with two perfectly conducting end plates. The resonator layers radii are denoted by r<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub>, p=1;2;3 are the boundaries of resonator layers, the radial thicknesses of the middle layers are Delta=r<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-r<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>, L is the axial size of the cylindrical resonator. All resonator layers are isotropic and they are characterized by complex permittivity epsiv<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nu</sub>=epsiv'<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nu</sub>(1+itandelta<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nu</sub>) and permeability mu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nu</sub>=mu'<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nu</sub>+imu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nu</sub> where nu =1, 2, 3 is the number of a resonator layer counted off from the resonator center and nu =4 is the number of the ambient medium, tandelta<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nu</sub> is loss tangent of the respective layer.

articleTitle: Intensity of Schumann Resonance: Universal Time and Local Time Variations
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Records of intensity of global electromagnetic resonance (Schumann resonance) contain two factors: one them depends of the local time and the other is the function of universal time that reflects the level of planetary thunderstorm activity. Three variants of a technique are considered, which allow for separation of local and universal time factors. Theses are applied toward the controlled numerical experiment and, finally, to the experimental records of distant observatories.

articleTitle: Mode Transformers on Longitudinal Diaphragms in Waveguides of Complex Cross Section
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this work the technique of longitudinal diaphragms is applied to MWT design based on four-ridge rectangular waveguides. The physical basis of mode transformation is discussed, the process of transformation of one propagating mode of the waveguide to another on different steps of the device is illustrated. The geometry of designed devices, pictures of electromagnetic waves distribution on transformer length and S-parameters, which are demonstrating wide bandwidth and good transformation efficiency, are shown.

articleTitle: Determination of the Upper Existence Domain of Operating Oscillation Modes in Space Harmonic Magnetrons
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In the course of development work on designing millimeter-wavelength magnetrons, many attempts had been made to achieve the regime of interaction between an electron flow and a spatial harmonic of one of the doublet-type oscillation modes. The techniques for establishing the causes that restricted the extent of oscillation in modes for the magnetic field non-pi-mode magnetron and determining the criterion for the upper boundary of their existence from the magnetic field can be employed as an integrated approach to selecting an oscillatory system parameter and calculating the magnetron's operating conditions from the magnetic field magnitude. The aim of computations is to determine the interaction space parameters that provide the required extent of the active oscillation mode region of an appropriate efficiency. Here, a description is given of the procedure for selection and subsequent test calculations of slow-wave structure parameters in a magnetron analog.

articleTitle: Comparison of 3-D and 2-D DCT Based Filtering of Multichannel Images
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A common feature of multichannel images of different origin and spectral bands is that they exhibit a high degree of mutual correlation of their components. At the same time, information content and noise properties in component images are more or less different. For the noise removal from such images, two general approaches are possible. The first one assumes component-wise (2-D) filtering; the second approach presumes vector (3-D) processing. Component wise filtering is, in general, simpler whilst 3-D processing that is able to take into account the inter-channel (inter-band) correlation of data is potentially more efficient.

articleTitle: The Quasi-Optical Waveguide on the Base of Dielectric-Foam Lens
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Measurements of the attenuation constant for the quasi-optical wave-guide designed and created on the basis of spherical lenses from dielectric-foam material is shown. The measurements were carried out in 3 mm range using polarization resonator. Results demonstrate that the specific losses of quasi-optical waveguide on the base of spherical lenses from dielectric-foam material are smaller in a few times than losses of standard metallic wave-guide. The small cross sizes of wave-guides (10 wavelengths), the offered type of quasi-optical wave-guides will be very perspective as the basis of input units for low-noise receiving systems of mm and sub-mm wavebands.

articleTitle: Quasioptical Polarization Attenuators in the Terahertz Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The attenuator on the basis of a hollow metal-dielectric waveguide of square cross-section 10 x 10 mm with similar polarizing gratings has been realized and tested. The largest attenuation of such an attenuator in the range 0.26 THz is 35 dB, attenuation scale reading A=(0...25)dB, initial attenuation is 0.3dB, VSWR is less than 1.05. The attenuator error is plusmn(0.1+ 0.02A)dB.

articleTitle: Fractal Analysis of Sea Ices Images
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The use of methods of the fractal analysis of radar allowed to define the ice-sea, sea-land borders. The application of quantization of the range of the received values of fractal dimensions allowed to carry out preliminary segmentation of the analyzed image by the selection of clusters of the set range of values of fractal dimensions. The line analysis of the initial image fractal dimensions can be used for estimating the degree of heterogeneity of the sea surface and selecting the ice-sea, sea-coast borders. The fractal analysis of images can be used for the development of safe routes of ships in Arctic.

articleTitle: Radiometric 5 mm Wavelength Receiver
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The development of high-sensitive direct detection radiometric modules with low-noise input amplifiers in 5 mm wave band is discussed. Two versions of modules have been developed. The module designed for atmospheric investigation operated in frequency band 56.6 plusmn 0.25 GHz and had temperature sensitivity 35 mK/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>. The module for biological investigation operated in frequency band 60...65 GHz and had temperature sensitivity 12 mK/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>.

articleTitle: The DRO with a Diffraction Grating Like a Chain of Coupled Resonators
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Test specimens of the 50...80 GHz diffraction radiation oscillator with a grating like a chain of coupled resonators - DRO(CCR) - are presented. The CW output power reaches 20 W at the accelerating voltage 3.6 kV, the spectral characteristics of the output signal are suited to modern studies in experimental physics. A possibility is shown for the further improvement of the DRO(CCR) performance in the 30 to 100 GHz frequency region.

articleTitle: A Planar Millimeter Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A millimeter wave antenna operating on the effect of surface to volume wave transformation is presented. Physically the antenna of the kind employs the plan electromagnetic wave diffraction by various periodic scatterers. Structurally it represents a source of nonuniform surface waves and a diffraction grating in the source field. The specialists joining the IRE NASU have gained enough research and development experience to produce various mm wave antennas of airborne, ground-based, scanning, single- and multi-beam functions.

articleTitle: The Precise Microwave Resonator Spectroscopy of Gases and Condensed Media
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, it was shown that reflectivity of reflector surfaces depends on the quality of thin metal reflecting layers and their coating. The influence is of course relatively larger for high reflective metals because of the smaller skin-depth. Results presented in this paper show low reflection loss for Planck reflector technology and very reasonable reflection losses for a metalized carbon fiber reinforced plastic (CFRP) technology. The latter technology has been measured at low temperature (liquid N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) and it is of interest to observe more than an expected factor '2' reduction in reflection loss. The importance of measurement of reflection loss has been discussed and the results presented or referred to in this paper confirm such a need.

articleTitle: Absorbing Boundary Condition for FDTD Modeling of Waveguides with Lossy Medium
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In order to solve diffraction problems with infinite structures (like waveguides) using FDTD needs some method to bound the numerical solution region with absorbing boundary condition imitating semi-infinite waveguide. In several such techniques are described that use either local conditions (ABC) or absorbing layer (PML), but most of these methods result in unacceptable reflection errors in vicinity of cutoff frequencies that may lead to significant errors in analysis of waveguide diffraction problems. In this work we are going to generalize the method onto the case of waveguide filled with lossy medium, provide numerical implementation, and analyze its performance.

articleTitle: Using of Geostationary Satellites Radiation for Determination of Hydrometeors Parameters
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The research method is based on determination of relation between X-band signal fluctuations of geostationary satellite and presence of hydrometeors on the path of radio propagation.

articleTitle: Microwave HTS Filter Based on Coupled Surface Wave Resonators
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The microwave properties of the 2-, 3- and 4-pole microwave filters, based on coupled surface wave resonators (SWR) made of high-temperature superconductor (HTS) film on dielectric substrate were investigated. The analysis of the systems is made by the partial wave synthesis (PWS) method. The normalized amplitude- frequency curve (AFC) is calculated for the Ka-band microwave filters.

articleTitle: Clinotron-Based Synthesized Oscillatiors for THz-Regions
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Advances in the design, realization, and investigation of the clinotron-based synthesized oscillators for THz-regions are considered. A high output power level, a fast frequency sweep, and a high frequency resolution are the characteristic features of the oscillators. The discussed synthesized oscillators benefit from advanced phase locking technique and an original high-voltage power supply. The corresponding technical solutions and test results are discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave detection on gated selectivelly doped semiconductor structure
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Microwave detectors on the base of asymmetrically shaped n-n junction of various semiconductor structures revealed possibility to detect electromagnetic radiation in very broad frequency range, i.e. from microwaves up to terahertz region. However, such detectors suffer from their low voltage sensitivity. Introduction of gate over asymmetrically shaped two dimensional electron gas (2DEG) channel in selectively doped structure essentially enhanced the sensitivity of diode, however, only in the X frequency range. Attempts to use the gated diodes at higher frequencies are demonstrated in this paper.

articleTitle: Low-Noise Microwave Devices: AlGaN/GaN High Electron Mobility Transistors and Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Noise and transport properties of state-of-the-art AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) heterostructures are analyzed with respect to high-frequency oscillator applications for different dissipated powers. The phase noise of a monolithic microwave integrated circuit oscillator based on the best choice AlGaN/GaN HEMT amplifier was investigated. A low level of the phase noise of the oscillator was registered. The up-conversion factor was found to be as low as 15 MHz/V for a frequency offset of 100 KHz, demonstrating that AlGaN/GaN HEMTs offer an excellent potential for a wide range of microwave applications.

articleTitle: Electrically-Triggered Microwave Filters on Coupled Modes
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this work, the structure of the waveguide-dielectric resonator with the combined ferrite-dielectric sandwich sample, on the basis of the design of electrically-tuned selective devices on microwaves, have been experimentally investigated. It was established that the effect of triggered coupling between the lowest types of modes exists not only at the presence of degeneration of the given mode types, but also at the channel selectivity on significant magnitude. The technique of the choice of electrically-tunable filters (ETFs) optimized operating mode resulted at transversal and longitudinal magnetizing mode of the ferrite sample of the filter.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Band Multi-Mirror Open Resonator. E- and H- Polarized Oscillations
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This work provides the experimental research results of E- and H-polarized oscillations of the complex multi-mirror open resonator (OR) , one of the mirrors of which is represented by the echelette reflective grating. The essential difference between the spectra of E- and H- polarized oscillations of complex open resonator (COR) is noted. It is evident that within the range of measurements performed for the H-polarization, only one oscillation mode is excited while in the case with the E-polarization there are excited several of such modes. In this case the self-collimation reflection from the echelette grating determines the conditions for excitation of the OR, which condition is the dispersive element forming up the OR spectrum. Some functional capabilities implied by the design of the suggested multi-mirror open resonant system are also discussed. The suggested multi-mirror open resonant system can find wide application in millimeter-wave band electronics for frequency stabilization of the electron-vacuum and solid-state devices.

articleTitle: Doppler-Polarimetric Approach to Microwave Remote Sensing of Precipitation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This study has shown that considered Doppler and polarization parameters of radar signal contain information on rain microstructure and turbulence intensity in weather object. The differential Doppler velocity of raindrops carries the important information on microstructure of rain and can be used in order to measure the rain intensity. However turbulence decreases this effect and should be taken into consideration as well. Application of independent turbulence-related variables can improve the reliability and accuracy of radar measurements in rain. Measurements of weather objects by Doppler-polarimetric radar can be very useful to solve wave propagation problems for the tasks of microwave remote sensing, communications and the radar's ability to detect targets embedded in high clutter background.

articleTitle: On the Possibility to Reduce the Power Consumption of FET-Based Amplifiers by the Drastic Reduction in Supply Voltages
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This paper reports on the successful development of an efficient method of the power consumption reducing without recourse either to cooling or to transistor periphery scaling. An approach proposed is based on applying the field-effect transistor (FET) having (initially, in saturated I-V region) an excessive-high cut-off-frequency and sacrificing their gain after changing to linear I-V region. Discussions of the theoretical grounding and experimental results of the implementation of this method to the design of low-noise amplifiers (LNAs) for radiofrequency (RF) as well as microwave bands, are discussed.

articleTitle: The Methods of Spectral Estimation of Signals Based on Kravchenko Weight Functions
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: It is known that an important topic is an intagral part of all classical spectral estimation methods is that of windowing. Windowing is used to control the effect of sidelobes in these spectral estimators. These effect are discussed in this report. The Welch method for improvement digital signal processing in combination with weighting functions (windows) Kravchenko was used. So, numeral experiments present the effectiveness of a new class weighting function (windows).

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Filters for Wireless Communications and Radar Applications - An Overview
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present an overview of the various microwave and mm-wave filter technologies for wireless systems, especially future high capacity broadband wireless data communication networks at 60 GHz, radio-over-fiber systems, 4G networks, vehicular systems and telematics transceivers.

articleTitle: The Account of Influence of Phase Errors of the Aperture of the Radio Telescope on Recovery of the Image of the Sun in 3 mm Range
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The nonstationary components of radiation of active areas of a solar surface are the important aim of investigation by solar radio astronomy at millimeter (mm) wave range. Radio astronomical observations of a solar surface determines the sizes, coordinates and the brightness temperature of active areas. The spatial resolution of the radio telescope limits the accuracy of definition of these parameters. It is determined by a width of directional diagram of antenna system. However there is possibility to increase a spatial resolution of radio astronomical researches at the expense of nonlinear iterative methods of recovery of the image.

articleTitle: Method of Magnetic Simulation Applied to Gliding Arc Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, it was proposed using a magnetic diagnostic method, to determine the variation of the length and the dynamic of gliding arc. This method, which is not intrusive, uses the hypothesis that the plasma and the reactor elements are similar to threadlike current segments. The magnetic induction created by the plasma and the circuit elements is measured in different sites outside of the reactor. To estimate the plasma shape and position, the measured magnetic inductions is compared to the one calculated using Biot-Savart law.

articleTitle: Statistical Model of the Signal Scattered from Sea Surface at the Grazing Feed Angles
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Experimentally obtained dependences of the lifetimes of the spikes and silent intervals in the signal scattered from the sea their spectrums and final probabilities of the existence including and simultaneous operation using several frequencies and polarizations allow using the proposed statistical model to fulfill the imitation of the noise conditions for the multifrequency and multipolarization radars. The proposed approach could be useful both for the theoretical analysis of the operating characteristics of the systems for the detection of the objects against a sea background and for the working-off the perspective algorithms of the radar information.

articleTitle: Microwaves Scattering from Synthesized Fractal Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This paper aims to report systematically and consistently about theoretical solution of scattering problem for the random fractal anisotropic surface using Kirchhoff approach for the first time, to calculate scattering indicatrixes for radio microwaves, to analyze ensemble of indicatrixes obtained. In this case for the fractal approaches we are introducing term 'scattering by the stochastic surface' that will be used in the future.

articleTitle: Diurnal Pattern of ELF Radio Signal Detected at the `Bellinshausen' Antarctic Station
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Diurnal amplitude variations were found in the man-made ELF radio wave recorded at the Antarctic station "Bellinshausen". The propagation path was 16.25 Mm long. Average level of the field corresponds to the literature data. Diurnal amplitude variations in the record arise from the day-night non-uniformity of the waveguide. The ambient day level is by 5 - 6 dB lower than that at the ambient night conditions in the vertical electric field component, it is by 4 - 5 dB lower in the horizontal magnetic field. Computational results are presented for the fields in the spherical Earth-ionosphere cavity with the 'whole day' and 'whole night' ionosphere models taken from literature. Model data contradict to observations indicating on inexact literature value of the phase velocity of radio waves. Model data match the experiment after the phase velocity is corrected by 10%. Since the 'whole day' and the 'whole night' ionosphere models do not account for the wave diffraction at the day-night interface, we conclude that more exact modeling is desirable.

articleTitle: Ka-Band Ground-Based Noise Waveform SAR
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: We present main results of design and investigations of Ka-band ground based interferometric SAR which uses continuous noise waveform as a probe signal and may operate in both monostatic and bistatic regimes. Synthetic aperture antennas enable to design a portable, light weight, easy to mount device with high speed of operation suitable for SAR imaging in quasi-real time while Ka-band noise waveform signals provide all-weather high resolution, high electromagnetic compatibility and interference immunity. Experiments have shown a rather high stability and repeatability of the measurements due to both the high quality of the equipment and advanced signal processing methods. The SAR system designed is an innovative instrument for solving new tasks of precise remote monitoring of various large objects, such as sealing of big halls, dams, bridges, TV towers, hangars, etc.

articleTitle: Influence of Shadowing Aperture by the Focal Module on Directional Characteristics of Reflector Antennas
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The present report aims to research the influence of the sizes of an irradiator on directivity, width of the main lobe and a level of side lobes of the sharp directional parabolic reflector antenna pattern. The analysis of directional characteristics of reflector antennas with big diameters of radiating aperture and other focal lengths results to the following important conclusions for practice: long focus reflector antennas are more wideband on gain and width of the main lobe than shortfocus; the more F/D, the less relative influence of shadowing on factor of gain and width of the main lobe; - the more F/D, the greater level of the maximal side lobe (both the minimal and average for any d/lambda); the more F/D, the more narrow the main lobe of the pattern.

articleTitle: Rectangular Microwaveguide with High-Tc Superconducting Wall
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The peculiarities of electrodynamic properties of metal waveguide of extremely small height (microwaveguide) have found in experiments. They show dependence of phase velocity or wavelength in waveguide on attenuation in waveguide caused by both finite surface impedance of walls and a height of waveguide. These effects are displayed even at small values of surface impedance Z<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>. Extremely-small-height waveguides are of interest for microwave technique, because their properties depend on impedance properties of wall material. Such a suitable material is high-Tc superconductors, impedance properties of which can be controlled by external factors, e.g. temperature, dc magnetic field or current, microwave or laser irradiation.

articleTitle: The Real-Time Phasemetric Microwave Navigation System for Position Detection and Drive Control of High-Speed Objects
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The concept of construction of navigation system for high-speed ground transport on the base of a phase metric method is grounded. It is shown, that the system provides high accuracy of position fixing of high-speed objects (of the order of one-two decimeters at speeds of moving up to 500 km/h and own linear dimensions about 100 m), sufficient for control of the linear engine and also allows to process the information going from measuring sensors and to give out control commands on executive units in a real time mode. The requirements to stability of frequency of basic and mobile microwaves-generators are determined. The offered built-in subsystem of diagnostic of working state of radio-navigation system promotes higher reliability of control system of high-speed transport mean and so higher safety of the all high-speed transportations.

articleTitle: Entire-Domain Method of Moments Analysis of Shielded Microstrip Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A full-wave analysis of a shielded microstrip line is presented based on the method of moments for entire-domain basis. A rigorous integral equation formulation incorporates a multilayered electric type Green's dyadic to deal with a multidielectric loading. Numerical results for microstrip line and suspended substrate microstrip line are obtained and compared with other available data.

articleTitle: SαS Process Location Parameter Adaptive Estimator Based on Data Censoring
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The task of location parameter estimation by means of adaptive censored procedure in SαS noise environment is considered. Based on the carried out research it is proposed to use the percentile coefficient of kurtosis and median absolute deviation as parameters able to describe processes with SαS pdf in case of absence of a priori knowledge about its statistical characteristics. The new formula is presented to evaluate the censoring parameter of the investigated estimator. Based on comparative analysis it is shown that the proposed adaptive procedure allows one to obtain the smallest variance among the considered robust and adaptive estimators for α ≪ 0.9. The proposed adaptive estimate can be put into basis of noise suppressing filter to be applied in image homogeneous regions in case of mixed noise.

articleTitle: Detailed Design of a 1 THz CW Gyrotron (Gyrotron FU CW III) Using a 20 T Superconducting Magnet
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The gyrotron consists of a 20 T superconducting magnet, a demountable gyrotron tube, a triode-type magnetron injection gun, and a sapphire output window. Additional coils are installed surrounding the electron gun centered at the emitter to adjust the beam radius and beam quality at the cavity region. The operation conditions of the cavity modes at second harmonic were investigated through the numerical experiments performed using a multi-mode time-dependent computer code.It is expected that the novel gyrotron will be able to the emit radiation at record of high frequency and unprecedented high output power for such frequency range.

articleTitle: Influence of Dielectric Materials on ATE Test Fixtures for High-Speed Digital Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: There are ever increasing challenges when developing test fixtures for high-speed applications using automated test equipment (ATE). This is due to the many variables and considerations that must go into developing characterization test fixtures for I/O cells in the 5 to 10 Gbps range. The purpose of these fixtures is to provide the best possible signal integrity of multi-gigabit data signals between the ATE and the device under test (DUT). One of the variables and considerations that needs to be controlled is the correct choice of dielectric material. Although there is a significant amount of work on dielectric loss for microwave applications, high-speed digital applications have different requirements given the broad frequency bandwidth of digital data patterns, as well as the high density of the I/O interconnects. Modern integrated circuits might have hundreds of differential high speed I/O cells requiring complex multilayer printed circuit boards (PCB) composed of different dielectric materials to be utilized for the test fixtures.

articleTitle: Influence of Low-Energetic Submillimeter Laser Radiation on Posttraumatic Skin Wounds
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, the next submillimeter radiation parameters with 0.337 mm wavelength: 5-7 irradiation procedures with energy density flow 0.4 mW/sm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was proposed for clinical aprobation of physiotherapeutic method.

articleTitle: Moment Method with Long Harmonic Subdomain Functions for Quasiperiodic Waveguiding Structures
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, physical effects of coupling of paraxial wave electromagnetic beam falling on surface with segment of spatially oscillating surface impedance and quasisurface (creeping) wave propagating along this surface are theoretically considered.

articleTitle: Millimeter and Submillimeter Semiconductor Hot Electron Bolometer
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this work Hg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Te based THz semiconductor hot electron bolometer (SHEB) with the direct detection for millimeter and submillimeter region is considered. In the proposed device the electromagnetic radiation heats only electrons in a narrow gap semiconductor without its lattice inertial heating. It is shown that using this narrow-gap semiconductor diode instead of a photoconductor as a THz detector seems promising because of smaller currents and larger resistances of p-n junctions.

articleTitle: Active Quasi-Optical Cavity Resonators Similar to Sinai and Bunimovich Billiards as Self-Excited Millimeter Wave System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The goal of the paper is to study experimentally the auto-oscillating systems based on quasi-optical 3D cavity resonators similar to instable Bunimovich and Sinai billiards and to detect the microwave generation in such systems activated by a Gunn diode. The concept of using this unstable resonator as a part of an active oscillating system is based on the following. The high quality factor resonator serves as an oscillating system in microwave oscillators. An increase of the quality factor of an oscillatory circuit leads to the reduction of excitation threshold of the oscillator and the increase of its frequency stability.

articleTitle: A New Method of Complex Dielectric Permittivity Determination
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The article proposes a new method of complex dielectric permittivity determination based on the use of surface wave resonator. This method is applied to fluorocarbon polymer-4, yttrium stabilized-zirconium and sapphire at frequency band 6-70 GHz.

articleTitle: Harmonic Filter Characteristics Optimization on the Basis of a Rectangular Waveguide with an Impedance Narrow Wall Partially Filled with Dielectric
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In the considered variant of the projective method the fields presented by proper functions of regular and non-regular waveguides are joined on these waveguides interfaces. The system of functional equations results. Taking into account the orthogonality of a regular waveguide proper functions, it was passed from the system of functional equations to the infinite system of linear heterogeneous algebraic equations. After certain mathematical transformations the number of unknowns in the system reduces. This system is solved by the reduction method. The problem of filter characteristics optimization is solved numerically in Turbo Pascal medium.
