As a result of numerical solution of a disperse equation, dependences of a non-regular waveguide propagation constants in a wide range of a surface impedance value change as well as dielectric plate parameters change on frequencies up to the third harmonic was shown. Calculations show that in such a structure propagation of both bulk and surface dielectric waves is possible. Quantity of propagation waves and frequency of their cut-off significantly depend on the surface impedance value and reactivity character as well as on dielectric plate parameters. Diffraction problem solution enables to optimize the filter characteristics. As a result of calculations dependences of main filter parameters were determined: reflection coefficient and transmission factor as well as attenuation constant on the complex impedance value and type of its reactivity; and power losses in a wide wave range including the first three harmonics.

articleTitle: Discrete Waveguide Attenuate on p - i - n Structures
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: We investigated the electrical and physical parameters and characteristics of the discrete waveguide attenuator of 8-mm wavelength range based on volume and integrating p-i-n-structures and the optimization was made. For experimental investigations of electrically controlled attenuators we have selected the samples of wanted parameters such as low-frequency control power, passing losses, switching rate, operating frequency range, control input currents and reverse voltage. We were investigating concrete electrically controlled attenuators layout where a circulator and two electricallly controlled switch were integrated.

articleTitle: Microwave Circuits Technique for Measuring Open Resonator Parameters Under Conditions of Hybrid Mode Excitation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A technique of measurement of unloaded Q-factors and resonance frequencies of the partial modes of a hybrid oscillation in a microwave resonator based on the measurement of total impedance of the resonator and interpretation of results with the method of equivalent circuits has been proposed.

articleTitle: The R-Function Method in the Investigation of the Problems of Diffraction of the Electromagnetic Waves on a System of Bodies
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This paper describes the R-function method in the investigation of the problems of diffraction of the electromagnetic waves on a system of bodies. The boundary problem of the diffraction theory in the field OmegaisinR<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>(x,y,z) which presents exterior of the one or several adjusted fields with piecewise-smooth boundary is considered. This approach can be used for a wide class of boundary problems with superconductive impedance.

articleTitle: Influence of Impact Ionization on Operation Efficiency of InN, GaN, AIN LSA-Diodes
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Analyzing the results of influence of impact ionization on operation of LSA diodes, possible conclusions were listed. Described LSA diodes on the basis of InN, GaN, AIN compounds have low efficiencies and small permissible overvoltage over threshold and on these factors worst then LSA diodes on the basis of gallium arsenide. For validly of the drift approach for developing impact ionization possible excess of an electric field strength above threshold in all LSA diodes on a basis of mentioned compounds is small, the efficiencies of oscillation also is small (for InN U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>/U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cr</sub> 1,6 ... 1,9 , so efficiency is as 3 ... 6 %; for GaN U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>/U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cr</sub> 1,4 ... 1,7 at efficiency 2 ... 4 %; for AlNU<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>/U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cr</sub> 1,06 ... 1,22 at efficiency 0,05 ... 0,23%). It is necessary to note, that all estimations are made for long diodes from 10 microns up to 1000 microns, on such lengths most favourably to implement LSA mode for reception of major power in cm- and mm - bands. If the impact ionization will develop in conformity with diffusion approach, performances of LSA diodes become quite comprehensible (for InN U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>/U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cr</sub> is 5 ... 5,85 at efficiency 11 ... 12%; for GaN U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>/U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cr</sub> is 4 ... 5 at efficiency 13 ... 14 %; for AIN U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</sub>/U<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">cr</sub> is 2,9 ... 3,3 at efficiency 3,2 ... 3,4 %). Taking into account high frequency opportunities of the described compounds, the received results will be quite good for LSA diodes for operation in a pulsed mode. The most perspective compounds for LSA diodes from the viewed (by efficiencies of oscillation) are InN and GaN (InN is better by quantity of overvoltage on the diode, GaN by dependence V(E), it is better by efficiency of oscillation).

articleTitle: Resonant and Broadband Microwave Characterization of Single-Walled Carbon Nanotubes
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: We report on microwave measurements of the complex permittivity of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWNT). The SWNT samples available for the study were a mixture of semiconducting and metallic nanotubes suspended with pluronic (F108) as a stabilizing surfactant agent, either in water or other (less lossy) liquid. Also powdered-form samples of SWNT and pluronic with varying conductivity were fully characterized. For broadband measurements, the shielded open-circuited transmission line technique was used. It is one of the variants of the coaxial transmission line based techniques, which have been used for dielectric properties measurements of solids and liquids for many years. Two different probes (7 mm and 3.5 mm with APC-7 and SMA connectors), both working in the frequency range of 50 MHz to 12 GHz, were utilized for the measurements. Inverse problem solving technique was employed to compute the complex permittivity from the measured Su complex reflection coefficient (labview controlled HP 8710 vector analyzer). The resonant technique measurements included the use of TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</sub> mode (3.4 GHz) and TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</sub> mode (6.5 GHz) dielectric resonators with cylindrical hole in the center of a dielectric disk. One of the modes should have electric energy concentrated predominantly in the direction perpendicular to the axis of static bias (z-axis) and the other one in the direction parallel to the axis of bias. For the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</sub> mode, the electric field has only an azimuthal component, which is perpendicular to the z-axis, while for the TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</sub> mode the electric field has both the axial and radial components. The axial component approaches maximum at the resonator axis while the radial component vanishes there. If the radius of a sample (radius of the inner hole) is relatively small, then the electric energy filling factor in the sample has predominantly the axial component. By employing the dc-electric field along the z-axis of the resonator, two components of a permittivity tensor were calculated using frequency and Q-factor of both modes. Simultaneous measurements of the resonant frequencies and the unloaded Q-factors of the two modes allowed the determination of the two components (parallel and perpendicular) of the complex permittivity tensor. Real part of the permittivity tensor was found by solving characteristic transcendental equations for the specific modes with respect to the appropriate tensor components. An excellent agreement between the complex permittivity data measured with broadband and resonator techniques was achieved. Results of the measurements of the dielectric constant and dielectric loss tangents versus dc bias for two liquid crystals will be presented. In addition, the mechanism of SWNT response to the dc electric field and also their anisotropy properties will be discussed. Some examples of potential electronic and bio-medical application of SWNT will be also shown.

articleTitle: Breakdowns in the Metal-Semimetal BiSb Point Contacts
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The current-voltage characteristics (CVC) and the breakdown effects in the metal-semimetal BiSb (bismuth and stibium alloys) point contacts have been investigated to determine the power rating of the radiation scattered by the sample. The CVCs of the contacts exhibit breakdowns provoking the appearance of the negative differential S-resistance areas. Based on the breakdown voltage magnitude one can determine the power rating of the radiation scattered by the sample.

articleTitle: Scattering Amplitude Error Analysis for the MoM Schemes in L2 Commonly Used for Solving a 2-D Scattering from Screens
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The scattering amplitude error estimation problem for practically used MoM solutions in L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> function space for scattering from 2-D screens is addressed. To this end, a rigorous Galerkin solution in L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> to logarithmically singular and hypersingular EFIE is used as a reference solution for scattering amplitude error estimation by benchmarking. This one requires substantially lower computational efforts than using of the same MoM algorithm but with very high mesh density as a reference solution. To many, the approach helps to avoid unpredictable errors due to the ill-conditioning connected with high mesh density for any MoM solution to the EFIE in L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Using the approach, the asymptotic decay rate of scattering amplitude error is investigated for some MoM algorithms widely used in practice.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Wave Absorption and Reflection by Carbon Nanotube Composites
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, electromagnetic wave absorption and reflection by carbon nanotube composites were studied. As the measurements show, examples presented for research have perspectives for being used for creation miniature fixed filters for tracking receivers, used as pre-and post-selectors and also in creation of frequency selective power limiters of matched loadings. The basic perspective of cheap carbon nanofibers- broadband radio absorbent materials.

articleTitle: Optimization of Polarizing Converters Based on the Cascade of Crossed Gratings
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The article studies the resonant regimes of the wave polarization conversion after the passage of a cascade of two or three crossed gratings. Two variants of three-grating crossing are considered.

articleTitle: The Procedure of Half-Wave Number Measurement at Resonant Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Waveguides methods of dielectric permeability measurement are widely used for their simplicity. Typical measurement cell in these methods is waveguide segment with flat dielectric layer (specimen). If dielectric without loss, VSWR (voltage standing wave ratio) frequency response for this cell has periodic, low damping character. Frequencies of VSWR minimum are resonant frequencies and frequencies of VSWR maximum are antiresonant frequencies. It gives possibility to produce method of dielectric permeability measurement, which uses means resonant or antiresonant frequencies only.

articleTitle: Study on SIS Mixers for "ALMA" Band-10
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This paper studies superconductor insulator superconductor (SIS) mixers for ALMA Band-10 project. The possible scheme of the ALMA Band-10 cartridge with balanced lens-antenna mixers is presented. The new balanced full-height waveguide SIS mixer comprises two equal mixer chips fabricated on quartz substrates. Each chip contains an RF circuit with hybrid twin-SIS junction NbTiN/Nb-AlO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>-Nb/Al. The preliminary experimental study of Band-10 receiver with a double-slot antenna SIS mixer mounted with a 10-mm immersion silicon lens is done to define an optimum layout of the tuning circuit and a combination of materials leading to the best performance of the SIS mixer.

articleTitle: Microwave Properties of Cuprate Superconductors in External Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this work, the intrinsic vortex viscosity in several cuprates are determined. It is confirmed that in REBCO (SmBCO) film the vortex viscosity is consistent with a conventional framework based on the Bardeen-Stephen model. In TBCCO a significantly smaller viscosity is observed, and possible test to assess the nature of this new effect is suggested.

articleTitle: The Broadband GaAs-Generator of MM - Range with Electronic Frequency Tuning
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The waveguide construction of the broadband GaAs-generator with electronic frequency tuning on a frequency range of 60...70 GHz with output of microwave power on the 2nd harmonic P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> = 10 mW is designed. Electronic tuning of frequency of the broadband GaAs-generator in a frequency range of 60...70 GHz has made 9 GHz.

articleTitle: Improvement of Fourier Modal Methods by Means of Non Conventional Coordinate Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The Fourier modal method has recently been improved with the idea of adaptive spatial resolution . By using a non-uniform sampling scheme that places more sampling points around the permittivity discontinuities, the total number of spatial harmonics required to achieve a given accuracy is significantly reduced. The idea of stretching thinner the space around the discontinuities is not entirely new in the larger context of rigorous numerical methods. What is new in our parametric approach as applied to gratings is that Maxwell's equations are written in the stretched coordinates under the covariant form.

articleTitle: Detectors of Ultra-Violet Radiation on Basis of ZnSe Schottky Diodes
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This works presents results of measuring the electric and photovoltaic characteristics of Schottky diodes designed on the basis of polycrystal ZnSe. The volt-ampere characteristics and the dark current of the diodes are discussed for its application as ultra-violet radiation photodetector.

articleTitle: Watermn's T Matrix and Quantum-Mechanical Transition Operator: Rigorous Derivation of Superposition T-Matrix Approach for Problem of Electromagnetic Scattering by System of Particles
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper we present rigorous and systematic derivation of the superposition T-matrix approach, which directly follows from the inhomogeneous wave equation. Starting from the complete integral solution of the inhomogeneous wave equation for a time harmonic field, we obtain first the equations for the Green's and transition operators. Then, expressing the free space dyadic Green's function in terms of spherical wave functions and separating variables, we find the equation for determining the matrix elements of transition loperator T for a system of particles using the matrix elements of T for isolated particles. We show that for divergence free electric field the matrix elements of T, expressed in spherical wave functions, directly connected to Waterman's T matrix.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Effect of Electromagnetic Absorption in Conditions of a Relative Motion of Components in He II
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A link of mechanical relative motion of normal and superfluid components of He II is determined and its electrical performances with use of the disk dielectric resonator (DDR) in a millimeter wave band of electromagnetic waves is made. The resonance frequency and Q-factor of the DDR into liquid helium are measured. The frequency and temperature dependence of the relative amplitude of electromagnetic wave traveling in He II are studied.

articleTitle: Microwave Spectrum of 2-Methylmalonaldehyde: Analysis of the Hydrogen-Transfer and Internal-Rotation Motions
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The paper presents a new experimental study of the microwave spectra of 2-MMA-dO [HO-CH=C(CH3)- CH=0] and 2-MMA-dl [DO-CH=C(CH3)-CH=0] isotopologues of the molecule. The new measurements were carried out by Fourier-transform microwave (FTMW) spectroscopy in the 8 GHz to 26 GHz frequency range and by conventional absorption spectroscopy in the 49 GHz to 149 GHz range. In the present work, we use a tunneling-rotational Hamiltonian based on a G,2m extended-group theoretical formalism to carry out global fits of 2578 2-MMA-dO transitions and 2552 2-MMA-dl transitions to measurement uncertainty, obtaining root-mean-square deviation of 0.015 MHz for both isotopologues. This presents a significant improvement in fitting accuracy over past attempts.

articleTitle: Application of Kravchenko Windows in Problems of Formation of the Radar Subsurface Layers Images by the Onboard Radar of Subsurface Sensing
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Usage of Kravchenko windows as envelopes of radar signals and form of a field pattern in the synthesized aperture allows to receive ambiguity functions of a system IPQ with optimum parameters of efficiency and to improve the quality of allocation of subsurface layers. The main attention is given to the analysis of ambiguity functions (AmF), radar signals and field pattern in the antenna with the synthesized aperture, fluidized classical windows and new Kravchenko windows. As a result of a simulation modeling the individual parameters of efficiency and integral parameter of efficiency (IPE) are obtained. Which analysis allows to reveal optimum weight functions used in radar station with the synthesized aperture (RSA) and modulation of radar signals.

articleTitle: Rainfall Statistics Over India
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Rainfall is one of the most important parameters in climatology, agriculture, weather modification and weather monitoring. Moreover, it is of immense interest in communication and link designing as above 10 GHz it attenuates the signal giving rise to interruption in wave propagation. In addition to this rain gives rise to cross polarization effect in communication systems where frequency reuse technique in used in order to increase channel capacity. Hence study of rainfall, the attenuation and cross polarization effect needs careful study. Attenuation prediction methods like ITU-R needs rainfall rates at less integration time. The Meteorological Departments, however, supply rainfall data at hourly interval. Hence a conversion formula from hourly to less integration time, say 1- minute or 15 minutes is needed. In this paper conversion formulae have been derived between hourly and 15 minutes rainfall rate over few stations in India. The rainfall data have been collected from India Meteorological Department, Pune. Regression coefficients have been derived between hourly and 15-minutes rainfall rate data.

articleTitle: Wavelet Analysis of the Signals with Peculiarities
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Wavelet analysis is a good tool for investigation of the signal's local peculiarities. Therefore the investigation of the wavelet analysis features appearing during the analyzing of the signals with peculiarities can be considered as actual. For the signal analysis the wavelets from the applied package Wavelet Toolbox 3.0 included in composition of the system of computer mathematics (SCM) MATLAB 7 were used.

articleTitle: Waves in the Periodic Stratified Media with the Anharmonic Law of Change of Permittivity
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, analysis of electromagnetic waves in periodic stratified media with anharmonic law of change of permittivity is carried out. The second order differential equations for amplitudes of transversal electromagnetic waves extending orthogonal to a direction of spatial heterogeneity are considered. The results obtained in this present work are applicable to quantum Bloch problem in a periodic field with anharmonic law of change.

articleTitle: Parametrically-Controlled Metallodielectric Magnetophotonic Crystals
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, it was shown that when used in 1D photonic and magnetophotonic crystals of millimeter and sub-millimeter range, thin (1..10 nm) metallic layers can be used to smoothen the zone structure and narrow the reflection bands. The electromagnetic energy is split into absorbed and reflected waves; the transmission is very low and can be neglected. Due to the very low ratio of it's optical depth (equal to it's geometrical depth divided by it's refractive index) to the wavelength, the metallic layer doesn't bring any additional pass or stop bands into the photonic crystal's (PC) zone structure. The strength of the spectrum smoothing and reflection band narrowing effect increases proportionally to the thickness and electric conductivity of the metallic layer, and decreases proportionally to the distance between the adjacent metallic layers (i.e. the summed thickness of the two paramagnetic/dielectric layers). The effect doesn't depend on permittivity and permeability of the metal (again, due to it's low optical depth). With metallodielectric magnetophotonic crystals it becomes possible to effectively shift the reflectivity zone(s) by means of external magnetic field. Tuning range will depend on the initial paramagnetic susceptibility and the width of the resonant curve.

articleTitle: Insights into the Problem of Reflection from Colloidal Systems: An Effective Medium Approach
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A colloid is defined as a system in which a dispersed phase is immersed in a homogeneous one. Here we model a colloidal system as a collection of a large number of identical spheres embedded at random in an otherwise homogeneous matrix. Recently developed effective-medium approach is used for the calculation of electromagnetic response in this model.

articleTitle: The Effect of Electromagnetic Field Extrusion in Sapphire Layered Semi-Ball Resonator Cell at Measurement of Complex Permittivity of High Loss Liquids
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, the effect of extrusion of the electromagnetic field in sapphire layered semi-ball resonator cell at measurement of different ratios of the real and imaginary complex permittivity of high loss liquids was investigated.

publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this work, a microwave spectrometer is built for the investigation of Cu and Ag atoms in Rydberg states with accuracy not worse than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. articleTitle: Peculiarities of 2 mm Orotron Operation on Second Space Harmonic
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: It is shown that the output power on the second space harmonic may be comparable with that on the first space harmonic at one-wave DRR regime. The possibility of the orotron OPS period increasing and tooth grating width increasing even operating only on the second space harmonic is demonstrated. The 3 times tooth grating width increase will allow to improve the hardness of small size OPS. Thus it is shown that the low- voltage orotrons may be effectives in THz wavelength range operating at one-wave DRR regime when their OPS parameters are optimized for high-order space harmonic operation. The work was partly fulfilled at the DPhS RAS "The radio physic problems" support, the "terahertz range development" division.

articleTitle: Operating Modes of Magnetron Auxiliary Cathode
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, theoretical investigations of the auxiliary cathode operation in magnetrons with secondary-emission cold cathode have been performed. It is shown that in the current magnetron design, the emission current of the auxiliary cathode depends on the temperature. It is also shown that a spatial-charge limited emission regime of the auxiliary cathode operation can be realized by introducing some changes to the magnetron design. Basing on the obtained results, a modification of the auxiliary cathode design is proposed. This modification provides the limitation of the auxiliary cathode emission by the spatial-charge, and, therefore, eliminates the temperature dependence of the emission current.

articleTitle: To the Question About Estimation of Residual Fluctuation of Signal on Output of Correlation Receiver of Noise Radar
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: It is shown in paper, that by virtue of random nature of signal being used in noise radars, a response on the output of correlator has an additional noise constituent unconnected with thermal noise of receiver. The value of this additional fluctuation is inversely proportional to the base of noise signal that it is necessary to take into account at development of noise radars. The value estimation of additional noise constituent in the present paper is done for stationary ergodic Gaussian noise signals with uniform and Gaussian spectrum.

articleTitle: Magnetic Management of Periodic Structure Parameters with the Band Gap
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A 1-D dielectric periodic structure which consisted of five periodic plane layers was placed into a standard waveguide with rectangular cross-section. Waveguides are fully shut and electromagnetic wave attenuation is secured up to -35 dB over the whole operating frequency range of the waveguide. Following the perturbation brought into the periodic structure the passing peak at frequency 44.6 GHz was formed in the band-gap. Transmission characteristics of the periodic structure and structure with defect are obtained. The approximate evaluation of the range of magnetic permeability change with the change of magnetic field is in good agreement with the experimental results.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Effects in the Layered Semiconductor Structures
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The nonlinear interaction of waves inside a two-dimensional layered periodic structure consisting of alternating semiconductor layers is studied. It was discovered that for the three-wave interaction processes the phase of a matrix nonlinear element changes depending upon the dispersion of dielectric permittivities of layers.

articleTitle: Occurrence of Phase Fluctuations of GPS Signals in the High Latitude Ionosphere During Geomagnetic Storms
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Dual-frequency measurements of the differential carrier phase of GPS L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> (f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>,= 1.575 GHz) and L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> = 1.228 GHz) signals have been used to study the development of phase fluctuations at high-latitude ionosphere during geomagnetic disturbances. The ionosphere irregularities are responsible for scintillations and phase fluctuations of GPS signals. Because of the depressive nature of the ionosphere the dual-frequency GPS phase measurements provide information about variations of the ionospheric total electron content (TEC). The paper analyses the occurrence of strong phase fluctuations of GPS observed at Antarctic stations. The fluctuations caused large scales ionospheric irregularities which were associated with occurrence of polar patches in TEC. The peculiarities of the latitude-longitudinal development of GPS signals phase fluctuations are described.

articleTitle: Square-Gradient Mechanism of Surface Scattering in Waveguides with Random Rough Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The goal of this contribution is to study competing mechanisms of surface scattering and their manifestation in the wave attenuation length (also known as the scattering length or the total mean-free-path corresponding to specific nth propagating mode) of multimode waveguides or electron conducting wires. We focus our attention on quasi-1D waveguides in which the total number of propagating modes (or conducting channels) is large. The roughness of the lower and upper boundaries of such waveguides are described, respectively, by the random functions. The relationship between those functions defines the waveguide's profile or configuration.

articleTitle: Current Instabilities under Millimeter and Submillimeter Electromagnetic Waves Heating in Semiconductors with Negative Differential Conductivity
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this article, the formation of static negative differential conductance (NDC) under simultaneous electron gas heating by high-frequency (HF) and static electric fields is studied. As in this case, the heating electromagnetic wave has a pronounced effect on appearance of NDC caused by the overheating mechanisms and on the type of the static current-voltage characteristic (CVC), as a whole.

articleTitle: V-Band Frequency Synthesizer for Irradiation of Josefson Array Junction in Voltage Unity Standard
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The V-band frequency synthesizer is presented including: a microwave voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO), a microstrip coupler, a 3-stage 25 dB centimeter-wave power amplifier, an active high-order IMPATT-diode multiplier, a band-pass filter, and an output isolator. The signal from the VCO tunable in the 7.00-7.10 GHz band throw a microstrip coupler goes to the power amplifier. After the amplification the signal passes to the multiplier, tuned to the 10th harmonic of the VCO operating frequency. This signal is amplified and then multiplied in 10 times by the IMPATT-diode multiplier.

articleTitle: Ubitron Under Magnetostatic Resonance Regime
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A possible chaotic behavior of electrons moving in the pump magnetic field of a hybrid planar ubitron may seriously influence its operating regimes. It turns out that some answers to the posed questions can be provided even in the framework of the linear theory.

articleTitle: Space Periodic Fields in Crossed-Field Devices
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This report aims to compare the motion trajectory of charged particles in crossed-field systems with both smooth and cavity anodes. To solve this problem, it is necessary to find the distribution of electrostatic potential in smooth and cavity anodes. Calculations of charged particle trajectory under these conditions are presented.

articleTitle: Interpretation of an Influence of the Transmitter and Receiver Bistatic SAR Tracks to Resolution
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Remote sensing of a surface by the bistatic model allows obtaining more information about surface conditions. Practically all remote sensing problems are solved on basis of ambiguity function analysis of a system. Here a qualitative variables of such system is determined by a resolution or by an ambiguity function width on the fixed level. The resolution of the bistatic SAR as the monostatic has an objects space discrimination in all directions even if is used unmodulated sounding signal and a selection degree mainly depends on a phase function variation rapidity where return signal is processed.

articleTitle: Mammographic Image Analysis by Use the Rank M-Type Radial Basis Function Network
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper we present the capability of the Rank M-Type Radial Basis Function (RMRBF) Neural Network in medical image processing applications.

articleTitle: Resonance effects due to exitation of the surface waves in periodically-modulated layered superconductors
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper the surface Josephson plasma wave (SJPW) excitation on the periodically-modulated layered superconductor is considered. It is shown that the absorption of the incident electromagnetic wave can be substantially increased at certain incident angles due to the resonance excitation of the surface waves. The optimal combinations of the parameters of the problem (modulation amplitude, wavelength, incident angle) corresponding to maximum SJPW excitation and the effect of the total suppression of specular reflection (TSSR) are found for a real medium (Bi2212).

articleTitle: Periodic Interface with/of Metamaterial: Resonant Absorption, Radiation, and Eigen Regimes
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The paper is focused at the study resonant phenomena arising in the process of electromagnetic waves interaction with metamaterials with periodic surface or with grating. Wide range of numerical experiments is performed on the base of accurate solution to boundary value problems. The peculiarities of diffraction characteristics and eigen waves and eigen frequencies in dispersive and anisotropic media have been revealed. The results, obtained in the study, have to help the understanding of the nature of diverse type of electromagnetic waves resonant transformation by the periodic surface with/of metamaterial.

articleTitle: Slit Resonance Based Rejection X-Band Coaxial Filter
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The original rejection filter design is presented. Based on the results of computational modeling the coaxial filter prototype has been manufactured and its characteristics have been investigated. The advantages of the proposed filter from the further stop band enhancement point of view are discussed.

articleTitle: Localization Length for One-Dimensional Array of Dielectric Bi-Layers with Correlated Positional Disorder
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The aim of this contribution is to obtain analytically the localization length for an array of periodic on average dielectric bi-layers of finite sizes, distributed according to correlated disorder potentials. To this end the widely used transfer-matrix approach generalizing it to random, arbitrarily correlated, systems is employed.

articleTitle: Electrodynamic Characteristics of the Dielectric Hemisphere Located Above the Surface of the Liquid
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The influence of the dielectric properties of liquid on electrodynamical characteristics of hemispheric dielectric resonator is studied. This article addresses the questions such as what type of mode (E or H) is more sensitive to disturbance from liquid, and what parameter of resonator (quality factor Q or frequency F) should be chosen to establish distinction in liquids. In a millimeter range it is possible to create a resonant measuring cell for analysis of dielectric properties of liquids with high dielectric losses in the form of the hemispherical dielectric resonator excited on whispering gallery type waves. To determine the imaginary part of dielectric permeability (epsiv") it is preferably to choose oscillations of H-type, while sensitivity a dielectric constant (epsiv') is practically identical for oscillations E- and H-type.

articleTitle: Complexity of Integral Algorithm for Calculation of Electromagnetic Field in Nonstationary Medium
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The paper is devoted to estimation of complexity of an algorithm for calculating of a nonlinear medium with parameters dependent on time.

articleTitle: High Order Spectral Estimation Methods in Ground Penetrating Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In ground penetrating radars (GPR) using stepped frequency continuous wave (SFCW), for an estimation of objects depth the inverse discrete Fourier-transformation (IDFT) of signals (image and real parts) on an output of the receiver is applied. As a result frequencies of spectral components corresponds to time delays (or to depths) of signals reflected from buried objects. In applications, in particular, in engineering geology surveys at the decision of problems with use of SFCW GPR, the spectrum width of a probing signal is choosing so that dispersive properties of medium not strongly deformed signals.

articleTitle: Elements of Chaotic Dynamics in Linear Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: It is shown that regimes with dynamical chaos are inherent not only to nonlinear system but they are widely represented in dynamics of linear systems.

articleTitle: Microvawe Discharge Properties in Goubau Line
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, analysis from experimental results showed some regularity in microwave discharge behavior and in signal propagation along transmission line. Microwave discharge in thin (conductor diameter three times less then oscillator wave length) single conductor transmission line represents erosion discharge of torch type. Material consumption and brightness temperature of conductor sputtering is determined by conductor material properties and oscillator power. Signal propagates in single conductor transmission line at conductor surface and its energy concentrates near the air-conductor surface. Different conductor bends do not lead to signal separation from conductor surface but they increase signal losses in transmission line skin layer. Conductor surface is heated during discharge process and is coated by a cinder that makes difficult to excite discharge again.

articleTitle: System Spectral Analysis of the Non-Linear Ultrawideband Signals
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, the investigation of usage features of new method called as the system spectral analysis for the non-linear UWB signal analysis is appeared to be actually.

articleTitle: About Possibility of Transferring of Height Power by Metal-Dielectric Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This paper describes the possibility of transferring by round straight corrugated waveguide (SCW) SHF power in units MW on wave HE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> confirms by several practical applications. articleTitle: Terahertz Low-Temperature Receivers for the Quasi-Optical Interferometers
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Low-temperature terahertz receivers intended for operation as a part of laser quasi-optical interferometers using basic transmission line as a hollow dielectric beam guide are designed. Examples of such receivers presented in this article include single-channel low-temperature receiver and four-channel low-temperature receiver.

articleTitle: Semiconductor Spherical Resonator of Millimeter Wave Band
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Necessity for research of high-order wave modes to solve the problems of solid-state electronic engineering for millimeter and submillimeter wavelengths. For study of similar waves, the approaching object is the spherical semiconductor resonator.

articleTitle: Superconducting 300 MHz Phased-Array for Magnetic Resonance Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This article reports on the development of superconducting phased-arrays by presenting a 300-MHz high critical temperature superconductors (HTS) array for imaging small animals for functional MRI of a rat brain and for high resolution imaging of spine injuries. Two four-element arrays are designed according to the requirements imposed by cryogenics and superconductor epitaxial technology limitations, with one made of copper and the other with HTS epitaxial YBa<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7-x</sub> thin films.
