articleTitle: Electrophysical Properties of Nematic Liquid Crystals under Stationary and Microwave Electric Fields
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The electrophysical properties of nematic liquid crystals under stationary and microwave electric fields was investigated in this paper. It was shown that substantial changes in electrodynamic properties of liquid crystal (LC) depending upon controlling parameters at low frequencies. Studies of such effects at microwave frequencies are of great interest and require further studies. The proposed approach can be also generalized to LC systems of other types, in particular, ferroelectric LC (chiral smectics-C), as well as LC with dispersed micro- and nanoparticles (carbon nanotubes, crystal ferroelectrics, magnetics, etc.).

articleTitle: The DRO with a Local Magnetostatic Inhomogeneity
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The low-voltage DRO development at the short-wave end of the mm region requires recognition of the prospects for enhancement of the DRO with a thick electron beam. For this purpose, the potential of "klinotron" excitation regime, magnetostatic field profiling and enhanced gratings is studied. The present work reports test specimens of the 50-80 GHz DRO whose focusing field carries a local magnetostatic inhomogeneity (LMI) in the interaction space.

articleTitle: Excitation of Broadband Signals in Coaxial TWT
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The theoretical analysis of a multifrequency regime of excitation of coaxial slow-wave structure shows perspectives of such transmission line for manufacturing of the microwave devices, capable to work simultaneously on several frequencies. Changing the energy of electron beam, it is possible to control the amplitude-frequency spectrum of output multifrequency signal. There are such energies of electrons beam for which it is realized simultaneous amplification of all waves. The complete efficiency of the amplifier at increasing number of launched waves remains high enough. Numerical calculations allowed to make conclusion about necessity of the account of excitation of combination components as due to their excitation and further amplification makes it possible to obtain a broadband output signal of device. In this case, an initial narrow-band signal is broaden, substantially due to amplification with high-frequency components.

articleTitle: The Contour Analysis of Low-Sized Complex-Shaped Objects Based on R-Functions, Atomic Functions and Wavelets
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The parameter processing of radar signals plays a great part in various fields of physics and engineering. The contemporary level of the development of the radar systems gives the opportunity to obtain rather complete information about an examining object. The great part in this process plays the processing of gained radar images, as they represent the main information, concerning the shape and the parameters of an object. Therefore, the main problems are the following: the rise of resolvability, the improvement of the quality of gained images as well as the creation of new fast-acting algorithms of radar information processing.

articleTitle: Filtration of the Radar Images by Filters with Weighting Coefficients of Classical and New Kravchenko Windows
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The radar image (RI), received with the help of radars with the synthesized aperture (RSA) is distorted by a speckle-noise.The purpose of activity is to analyze effect of the size of a sliding window on outcomes of a filtration.

articleTitle: Operating Particularities of the HCN-Laser Terahertz Frequencies Range with the Anomalous Secondary Emission Cathode
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: For increasing HCN-laser efficiency is undertaken attempt realize cathode with anomalous (Makers effect) secondary emission (ASE). Its created original design of the cathode with anomalous emission characteristic - small cathode voltage drop and corresponding reduction of the general voltage drop on discharge. In the course of experimental studies of the laser structure of the cathode with ASE was optimized. For practical application was to design the graphite cylindrical hollow cathode with ASE, providing increasing HCN-laser efficiency.

articleTitle: Possibilities of Surface Relief Determination by Photometric Method in Millimeter and Submillimeter Wavelength Range
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, possibilities of planet surface relief determination by photometric method in millimeter and submillimeter wavelength range were studied. Considered in this paper was the case where the initial images were acquired with a side-looking radar, focusing attention upon the issue of informativity of obtained image series relative to the relief desired.

articleTitle: Terahertz Gas-Discharge Laser with Additional Dicharge Section
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This work presents a method of increasing the power and efficiency of terahertz gas-discharge lasers by application of additional discharge section for synthesis of active substance in HCN discharge lasers. It is expedient to optimize of intensity of pumping out of such lasers together with optimization of volume of additional discharge section.

articleTitle: Left-Handed Magnetostatic Surface Waves
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The characteristics of magnetostatic surface waves at microwave frequencies in a layered structure of left- handed material film and a semi-infinite linear ferrite substrate have been investigated. The effects of the applied external magnetic field around the proposed region have also been examined.

articleTitle: Mikrowave Propagation Factor at Small Grazing Angle Over Sea
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: On the basis of analysis of extensive experimental data of our researches on the centimeter and millimeter radiowave propagation above a sea and land and results was formulated the conception that heights are single meters above a marine surface with agitation for description of the field it is necessary to utillize a diffraction model but not method of tangent plane (MTP). The lower limit bound of strict application of MTP is determined two criteria: 1. by absence of shadings of elements that reflect to a point observation of the field, its roughnesses; 2. by a limit on the minimum value of the glancing angle from the convex element of roughnesses. After such conclusion obtained from test data analysis, we have applied the proposed DCT based filter to processing real life X-band side look aperture radar (SLAR) images. Thus, we demonstrated that the proposed adaptive DCT-based filter is rather efficient for removing non-stationary noise in selected test applications.

articleTitle: Modeling of Impulse Photomultiplier on Basis of PN-I-PN Structure with Avalanche P-N Junctions
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: It was shown in this paper that the dynamic range of the amplification of avalanche-cascade multiplication (ACPM) achieves 80 dB and limited by of spatial charge of carrier mobility. Fast-acting of ACPM makes a few ten nanoseconds and is determined by the number of cascade of multiplication and time of drift of carriers in a pn-i-pn structure. ACPM is a low-noise device - his power equivalent to noise (NEP) more than on an order less NEP avalanche photodiode (APD). ACPM is intended for amplification of impulses of photocurrent, duration of which does not exceed the half-cycle of structure, and period of their following more time fast-acting. Thus, ACPM is the perspective impulsive photomultiplier of new type, principle of action of which is based on the avalanche-cascade multiplication of primary photocurrent.

articleTitle: Effect of Pulse Magnetic Field on Microwave Properties of YBCO Thin Film Strip-Line Resonator
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This work investigates the effect of single pulse magnetic field on microwave characteristics of YBCO thin film strip-line resonator such as the quality factor Q and resonant frequency F, and their evolution during the flux creep process at different temperatures and input power levels. It was shown that: (i) induced magnetic flux and screening dc current, resulting from the pulse action, noticeably change both resonant frequency and quality factor; (ii) relaxation of the trapped flux and pulse-induced current, caused by flux creep process (at rather high temperatures) lead to time evolution of these resonator characteristics. This relaxation proceeds in two stages: quick relaxation during the first 1-2 seconds (at T=78 K) and long term (logarithmic) relaxation. The rate of long term relaxation increases with temperature increase; on the other hand it doesn't depend on the input power level.

articleTitle: Scanning Radiometry Measuring Complex with Programmed Numerical Control
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The radiometry measuring complex equipped by the improved circuit of numerical control by support-rotating mechanism forms the radiometry images of the ground-based objects in the wide range of scanning speeds with high positioning exactness. High exactness of support-rotating mechanism allows applying for the pictures forming of largenesses antenna with high spatial resolution. In addition, this device allows making the high-fidelity measuring of antenna directivity diagram. The objects images formed by a radiometry complex in the millimeter and infra-red wave's bands distinguish by the high contrasting, image clear edges. A radiometry complex allows forming the images under the various angles of elevation, up to vertical.

articleTitle: Development of High Efficient Technological Gyrotron with Depressed Collector
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: High power microwave radiation is applied for an ever increasing range of programs aimed to create materials with new qualities. The gyrotron complexes for microwave material processing created at IAP RAS jointly with GYCOM Ltd. do not have any analogues with similar functional capabilities but they are less effective than decimeter wavelength systems. The complexes use gyrotrons at the second cyclotron harmonic with the efficiency output of 30-40% as a source of microwave radiation. The expansion of gyrodevice based systems to novel technology and industrial applications requires further efficiency increase. The electron beam energy recovery is one of the most effective methods to achieve this. The presented results have been used for development of high efficiency harmonic gyrotron with depressed collector.

articleTitle: Effect of Focusing Magnetic Field on Electron-Wave Processes in Amplifier on Smith-Parsell Effect
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The model of amplifier on Smith-Parsell effect the based on are opened waveguide (OW) has been offered, are carried out theoretical and experimental researches of such system. The analyses physical processes of interaction EB with fields system in a mode of the diffraction radiation (Smith-Parsell radiation) specify an opportunity of build-up the amplifier with the distributed interaction on body waves. However the given theoretical model does not take into account effect of a finite value intensity of focalizing magnetic field on the electron-wave processes occurring in the amplifier, as has spotted subjects of this work.

articleTitle: On Influence of 2D Inhomogeneity on Electromagnetic Mode Conversion Near the Cut_Off Surfaces in Magnetized Plasmas
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Most of the analytical results in the theory of OX conversion are obtained in a slab geometry, in which the magnetic field is uniform and 1D spatial inhomogeneity is related to a constant plasma density gradient. An extended analytical study of the OX wave coupling in 2D geometry has been performed previously in our works, which are briefly summarized in the current communication.

articleTitle: Microwave Penetration and Magnetic Resonance in Cluster-Layered Fe/Cr Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The article investigates the magnetic field dependence of microwave penetration coefficient through the Fe/Cr nanostructures and superlattices with ultrathin iron layers. The samples are grown by molecular beam epitaxy method. The magnetization curves have been measured in the fields up to 18 kOe. The magnetoresistance of the nanostructures are measured ad DC.

articleTitle: Polarization Phase Shifters and Spiraphase-Type Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, the application of the polarization principle of phase changing permits to design low-loss phase shifters operating at microwave frequencies with the total loss less than 1 dB at Ka band and less than 0.5 dB at X-band. The spiraphase-type arrays based on the proposed phase shifting element demonstrate the wide-angle scanning combined with the acceptable conversion characteristics.

articleTitle: Variable Beam Width MMW Band Antenna
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Structure chart of offered variable beam width antenna for ground-based station is presented. Antenna contains a set of N (N>2) diffraction grating distributed on rotating cylinder (drum) and a linear dielectric wave-guide located along focal axes of the receiving parabolic-cylindrical reflector. Antenna operation, when it is amounting into communication line ground-based station, could be executed on the base of real-time UAV position data, which could be obtained, for example, from GPS receivers located in both stations, or contrary on the base of output information obtained from ground based UAV tracking.

articleTitle: Results of Laboratory Test of Immunity of Correlator Affected by Active Continuous Interferences at the Processing of Wideband Noise Pulses Sequences
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Works concern to computer modeling of immunity of noise and LFM radars affected by single-frequency interference that is its influence on a form of output correlation effect depending on time of accumulation. The different influence of single-frequency interference is examined for both noise and LFM-signals as well as SAR-image. Advantage of application of matched correlating processing of a noise signal is quality shown for neutralization of influence of single-frequency interferences by means of increase of accumulation time. The presented experimental investigation of immunity of noise radar affected by wideband or/and single-frequency interference. The aim of the presented work is: estimation of immunity of correlator matched with a noise pulse under influence of active (mutual and intentional) continuous interferences with application of local criterion of immunity at signal level; detection of the decorrelating factors bringing with a real correlator.

articleTitle: Grazing Incidence Reflectivity of High-Tc Superconductors: MM Wave Technique, a New Approach to Study and First Results
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The method allows investigation of the superconductors conductivity of which changes under different external conditions such as temperature, magnetic field, etc. The possibility to obtain such HTS characteristics as complex conductivity or surface impedance using measured complex reflection coefficient, calibrated by absolute values of reflection coefficient of the known materials, has been shown. The applicability of the method to investigating peculiarities of microwave properties of unconventional superconductors in normal state was shown as well.

articleTitle: Technical Advances in Spin Labelling EPR
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: EPR-Techniques have experienced some kind of revival and increased interest, especially in connection with biological and biomedical applications of EPR. The main aim is to get information on the localization of the spin label and its interaction with the substrate molecule. CW-saturation experiments as well as pulse techniques like saturation-recovery-ELDOR and dead-time-free double electron-electron resonance can be used for this purpose. All these techniques require some special hardware development in addition to our routine and research EPR spectrometers. One of the most promising applications of EPR imaging in oximetry.

articleTitle: Order Statistics Based Algorithms in Filtering of 2D-3D Images and Objects
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Novel vector rank M-type K-nearest neighbor filters are adapted for multichannel image processing. Ultrasound images are contaminated by impulsive noise and 3-D filtering algorithms are applied.

articleTitle: Using of PSTD-Method and Transmission Matrixes for Research of Light Diffraction by Periodic Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The article develops method for solving diffraction problems on real optical planar structures. The periodic structure used in the study consists of aluminium and silica. The wavelength dependences of the permittivities of both materials are measured. The combined pseudo-spectral time domain-finite differences time domain (PSTD-FDTD) technique is used to solve the diffraction problem.

articleTitle: Resonance properties and energetic parameters of transverse slots in a waveguide with a dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The numerical investigation of physical properties of transversal slots in a rectangular waveguide partially filled with dielectric was carried out on the base of the excitation problem solution with the eigen waves method. It was shown that it is possible to find geometric and electrical parameters of the system which provide the distance between the adjacent co-phased resonance slots less than a wavelength in the free space. The level of the radiation and reflection coefficients depends on epsiv and the layer thickness. It is possible to obtain the reflection coefficient less than one in the case of the full filling the waveguide with dielectric. Thus the transverse slots in the waveguide considered can be used for construction of waveguide-slot resonance antennas radiating the field with horizontal polarization.

articleTitle: Diffraction Radiation Antenna for 8-mm Waveband Radar Meant for Airfield Observation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: High-resolution millimeter wave radars become an essential part of ground safety systems. Among them, radar systems for airfield traffic control are of special interest. The diffraction radiation antenna has been designed for it, using novel technology. The antenna consists of a ridged dielectric waveguide, diffraction grating, and focusing lens. The eigenwave of the ridged dielectric waveguide excites resonant oscillations in the elements of the diffraction grating.

articleTitle: A Novel Microwave High-Temperature Superconducting Reaction-Type Transmitting Filter for Mobile Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A novel split open-ring reaction-type construction technique to achieve high power-handling capability for High-temperature superconducting (HTS) filters is presented. The purpose of this filter is to suppress the adjacent noise generated by transmitting power amplifiers for mobile base stations. First, it is explained that reaction-type filters are suitable for high power transmission. Secondly, novel split open-ring resonators, which reduce the maximum current density while maintaining high Q-factors are proposed. Current density dispersion effects are evaluated under the same coupling coefficient. Finally, a 5 GHz three-pole reaction-type filter using split open-ring resonators is designed. The frequency characteristics of the filter are investigated by using the method of moments. The results predict that the filter realizes both a higher power-handling capability than that of transmission-type filters and a better skirt property than existing HTS filters using dual-mode resonators.

articleTitle: Photobiostimulation Effects Caused by Low Level Ultra-High Frequiency (v=2.45GHZ) and Laser Radiation (λ=650 NM and λ=850 NM) in the Growth Stimulus of Biological Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This paper has as principal objective to determine the value of some parameters of light that are determinants in the activation or inhibition of the growth stimulus in a biological system. In this case intensity and dose, as important parameters, were considered. Semiconductor and GaAIAs lasers with λ=650 nm were used to irradiate the biological systems. In the first part of this study three different biological systems were defined. In the first biological system Triticum aestivum L (wheat) seeds were used; for the second biological system Cucumis sativus L (cucumber) seeds were used, and finally for the third biological system human fibroblasts were used. The responses of the three biological systems were analyzed using statistical processes when intensity and dose were varied. The results obtained indicate that when the appropriate light parameters are used activation or inhibition can occur.

articleTitle: Development of CW THz gyrotrons in FIR FU
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The new gyrotron series in FIR FU, so-called Gyrotron FU CW Series is being developed for application to high power THz technologies. Gyrotron FU CW II with an 8 T liquid He free superconducting magnet, the second gyrotron of the series, has been constructed and the operation test was successfully carried out. It will be used for enhancing the sensitivity of 600 MHz proton-NMR by use of Dynamic Nuclear Polarization (DNP). The designed operation mode of the gyrotron is TE2,6 at the second harmonic. The corresponding frequency is 394.6 GHz. The real operation frequency is 394.3 GHz at TE06 mode, because of fabrication error of the diameter of the cavity. The operation is in complete CW at the output power of around 30 W or higher at the TE06 cavity mode. There are many other operation modes at the fundamental and the second harmonic. Typical output power of the fundamental and the second harmonic are higher than 100 W and 20 W, respectively. The thirs gyrotron, Gyrotron FU CW III with 20 T superconducting magnet has already been designed and the construction has been almost completed. The operation test will start soon. Such a present status of high frequency gyrotrons in FIR FU will be introduced.

articleTitle: Superscars in Barrier Billiard - Phenomenon Induced by Diffraction
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Here is presented an experimental investigation of superscars in a quantum barrier billiard.The experimental observation of the superscars requires (i) the detection of eigenmodes at sufficiently high quantum numbers N and (ii) the resolution of all modes up to these quantum numbers.

articleTitle: Full-Wave Analysis of Waveguides Periodically Loaded with Irises
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper we have proposed a full-wave approach for the dispersion analysis of waveguides periodically loaded with arbitrary shaped irises. It is based on the boundary integral equation method, mode matching technique and S-matrix method and has been implemented in a computer code. The data calculated by the code are in accordance with published data.

articleTitle: Microwave Characterization of Bulk Ferroelectrics and Relaxors using Composite Dielectric Resonator
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A method based on a composite cylindrical dielectric resonator (DR) to characterize the dielectric permittivity and losses in the microwave range of a ferroelectrics and relaxors is developed and set up. Resonance frequencies and Q-factors of the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</sub> mode and TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">021</sub> mode of the composite DR versus dielectric loss of the sample with different permittivity is studied. Temperature dependences of the dielectric permittivity and loss of ferroelectric Ba<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</sub>Sr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</sub>TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> ceramics with coarse and fine grains and of relaxor ceramics PMN and Ba<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>La<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>Ti<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sub> at high frequencies and microwaves are measured.

articleTitle: H F W Diagnostic of the Microwave Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The uniform linear array in a transfer mode is investigated. On a measuring platform are present echo in the form of re-reflected probing signal from the ground and local subjects. It is required to define: transfer ratio of phase shifters (PS) in all of them conditions and changes of reflectance in emitters track, caused by mutual coupling of emitters, at scanning a beam of phased array .

articleTitle: Spatial Correlation of Linear and Nonlinear Electron Transport in a Superconducting Microwave Resonator: Laser Scanning Microscopy Analysis
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Nonlinear microwave response of high-T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub> superconductors (HTS) at high circulating power limits the applicability of HTS resonators to the few-mW level. Methods of spatially-resolved RF analysis are needed to identify the nonlinear sources as well as to establish their relative influence on the global response. In this work laser scanning microscopy is used to analyze the spatial correlation of linear and nonlinear electron transport in the superconducting YBCO film microwave resonator.

articleTitle: Microwave Generation of HTS Josephson Junction Integrated in a Microwave System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Microwave properties of the surface wave resonator (SWR) consist of high-temperature superconductor (HTS) film on dielectric substrate were investigated. The analysis of the systems is made for a film with an array of HTS Josephson junctions (JJ). In the last case it was revealed the Josephson junction synchronization effect, occurred under the influence of electromagnetic field (EMF) of the SWR. Due to this effect it is possible to make devices with synchronized array of junctions. The Josephson generation of HTS JJ array, embedded in the SWR is investigated in the X- and Ka-band.

articleTitle: Quantum Cascade Laser Spectroscopy, Trace Gas Analysis to Non-Linear Optics
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: This paper reviews quantum cascade laser spectroscopy and its applications for trace gas sensing and non-linear optics. The development of pulsed lasers for these applications are discussed focusing on the intra-pulse method. The operation of the quantum cascade laser spectrometer is investigated experimentally and by computer solutions of Maxwell-Bloch equations.

articleTitle: Efficient Electrical Electron Spin Injection from Ferromagnetic Metals in Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A spin-polarized electron transport in a double-barrier tunneling nanostructure which contains CoFe/MgO spin injector has been investigated. The electron spin polarization ratio was calculated in the framework of the two-band model of free electrons in ferromagnetic metal contact. The influence of the bias voltage and tunnel barrier height on the spin polarization ratio of the electron current as well as the optimal bias voltage and the nanostructure parameters, which ensures the efficient electrical electron spin injection into nanostructures, were also determined.

articleTitle: Evolution of C-Method within the Frames of Diffraction Grating Theory Development in France
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: With C method diffraction by a surface is solved like in quantum mechanics by an eigenvectors method. Operators contain explicitly boundaries as functional parameters. It is possible to use all tools of quantum mechanics matrices associated to operators, perturbation method , uncertainty principle and many others. This lead to a very efficient modeling.

articleTitle: Magnetic Tunnel Junctions with Assymetric Barriers
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this paper, magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) with a low asymmetric barrier are presented. These MTJs can be described by the two-band model of free electrons in ferromagnetic electrodes. The influence of image forces on the tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) and on the electron current density in MTJs are taken into account. It is shown that the electron current density in the low barrier MTJs is quite enough for the current-driven magnetization switching of the ferromagnetic electrodes. The results obtained here extend considerably the knowledge about the physics of tunnel processes in magnetic nanostructures and can be used for developing MTJs with desired parameters.

articleTitle: A Parallel Spectrum Analyzer Based on a Multi Channel Direct Conversion Receiver
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: A spectrum analyzer is designed and constructed on the base of a direct conversion receiver. A millimeter-wave heterodyne receiver is applied to expand input frequency range of the spectrum analyzer. At present the spectrum analyzer operates at frequencies between 149 and 212 MHz, i.e. 64 channels with 1 MHz resolution.

articleTitle: Use of the Cast Amorphous Microwire Witch Natural Ferromagnetic Resonance for High Frequencies Radioabsorbing Materials and Screens
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The radio absorption properties of these cast amorphous microwire (produced by Ulitovsky-Taylor method) appear around the frequency of natural ferromagnetic resonance. In that range, dispersion is observed in the real and imaginary components of relative magnetic permeability. In summary, glass-coated amorphous microwires, which have been used to fabricate composites in the form of planar radio absorbing screens less then 2 mm thick operating efficiently in the range 8-11 GHz. It is shown that the microwires under consideration are of certain technological interest for radio-absorption. The application of thinner microwire can improve the characteristics of the screens by increasing the effective conductivity of the simple. Knowing the width of the dispersion curve of magnetic permeability, one can use various microwires more efficiently for design of radar-absorbing materials.

articleTitle: The Non-Equidistant Directional Couplers on the Basis of Least Ordered Strings
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Among a variety of SHF devices types a promising trend of SHF devices with non-equidistant components arrangement is being developed. The non-equidistant components arrangement application improves SHF devices technological effectiveness, simplifies their practical realization and, besides, according to the law of non-equidistant components arrangement it gives a number of other advantages. In addition, equicomponential non-equidistant directional coupler (NonEDC) besides their technological effectiveness possesses such an advantage as the lack of amplitude distribution dispersion conditioned by coupling components (CCs) dimensions.

articleTitle: Resonant phenomena in the system of coupled waveguide branches
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: In this work resonant phenomena in half-open waveguide structures of a different section form have been considered. It is defined that under certain conditions there exists a mode of natural oscillations. That is why intersecting waveguides must be at the setoff resonance frequency.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Study of Hybrid Superconducting Heterostructures with Magnetic Active Interlayer
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)

Critical current density was 10 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> through 50 nm thick Ca<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Sr<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>CuO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> layer, and increased for thinner layers. Half- integer Shapiro steps and detector responses were observed for the most of heterostructures. Current phase relations of the heterostructures deviated from sinusoidal with 10divide40% portion of the second harmonic.

articleTitle: Magneto-Milliwave Isotherapy
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: The method of medical treatment of many diseases on principle of aequalia aequalibus curentur changed from eastern to western therapy, at the same time the biochemical and biophysical izotherapy are distinguished. In the first case the preparations (autonozods) made from different substances of patient's organism, for example, from his own blood and others are used. In the second case the prepared electromagnetic radiation from a bioobject is put in the patient's organism. The spectral structure of this electromagnetic radiation determines the character of metabolism in the patient's organism and it's source is the patient's organism, so the oscillation model of therapy realizes.

articleTitle: Optimal Sectional Taper for Circular Metal-Dielectric Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Using results of various researches, we have theoretically calculated geometrical parameters of OSWT for MDW having various sections, and also losses in such taper. It is possible to see, that the least losses in parabolic taper, and three-section taper is close on the properties to "ideal" - parabolic taper. Given theoretical results can be used in development such tapers for quasioptical transmission lines millimeter and submillimeter wave range.

articleTitle: Micromachined Microwave Components for Communications and Radar
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Summary form only given. Complex passive microwave components at frequencies above around 50 GHz are difficult to build because of their small size and high fabrication tolerances required. Micromachining is one technique which can achieve the desired results, and this paper will describe a new micromachining technique together with the microwave design and experimental tests. The applications considered are car communication and radar systems. A SU8 thick photo resist is used to produce a square coaxial cable filter, the filter design fabrication and experimental results will be given. The cable is made of five metal coated layers of SU8 bonded together to form a single component, the SU8 has the advantage that it can form mechanical components up to many hundreds of microns thick whilst still retaining very accurate control over the size of the features. The use of SU8 in this manner eliminates radiation loss and dielectric loss and optimize the conductor loss of the passive circuits; it is therefore useful when the ultimate performance of passive circuits is required.

articleTitle: Separation of the Instantaneous and Dynamic Polarizations in Studies of Dispersive Dielectrics Kharkov, Ukraine, June 25-30, 2007
publicationTitle: 2007 International Kharkov Symposium Physics and Engrg. of Millimeter and Sub-Millimeter Waves (MSMW)
abstract: Forced oscillations are studied in a closed resonator filled with a polar dielectric. Time-dependent current density is installed in Maxwell's equations as an externally forced signal source. The latter can be an arbitrary integrable function of time. The system of Maxwell's equations (with ∂<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</sub>) is solved simultaneously with Debye equation for the polarization vector, which plays role of a dynamic constitutive relation between the polarization vector and the electric field. The electromagnetic field vectors are presented as modal expansions in terms of the solenoidal and irrotational modes both with time-dependent modal amplitudes. A set of evolutionary differential equations for the modal amplitudes, supplemented with appropriate initial conditions, is derived and solved explicitly. The instantaneous and dynamic component parts of polarization are present in the solutions separately.
